# Blueprint requirement catalogue

Generated by `qip blueprint render` from
`docs/blueprint/requirements/*.json`. **Do not edit this file by hand**:
edit the JSON and re-render. `qip blueprint check` fails when this view is stale.

Sources and precedence: [README.md](README.md). Architecture of record:
ADR 0099.

**1566 requirements** in 31 domains. Priority: P0 629, P1 579, P2 226, P3 132.

P0 covers safety and correctness invariants, contracts, and the exit criteria of the
foundation phases. P1 covers the cognitive data loop, the tick lake and replay,
multi-asset capital and risk, and multi-region. P2 covers arbitrage, market making,
quantum, prediction and commerce, and AGI autonomy. P3 covers open-ended expansion
and causal agency.

## Policy flags

A flag marks a requirement that cannot be fully met without something a standing
decision refuses. The conflict register is in ADR 0099.

| Flag | Requirements | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `LIVE_CAPITAL` | 69 | needs live orders or real money movement; refused (ADR 0003/0021, conflict C1) |
| `EXTERNAL_ACTION` | 74 | needs the platform to act on the outside world; refused (C1) |
| `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | 107 | needs a crate beyond serde/serde_json (C2) |
| `MANAGED_SERVICE` | 312 | needs a GCP managed data/AI service (C4) |
| `KUBERNETES` | 87 | needs GKE / Argo / service mesh (C3) |
| `NON_RUST` | 76 | needs a non-Rust runtime (C5) |
| `MULTI_REPO` | 11 | needs a multi-repository split (C6, declined) |
| `MULTI_REGION` | 132 | needs more than one region (C8) |
| `COST` | 94 | implies significant recurring spend (C8) |

| CONTRACT-037 | P0 | contract | **StreamPolicy contract fields** — A StreamPolicy carries: partition key; replication factor; ack policy; retention; durability/QoS class; byte and message limits; consumer lag threshold; mirroring policy; overload/shedding behavior; and entitlement. |  | unit: Creating a stream without a StreamPolicy, or with a policy missing any listed field, is refused. Under overload a telemetry-class stream sheds records and a control-class stream does not. | v11.6 p39 §27 Core Contracts Between Brains — StreamPolicy |
| CONTRACT-038 | P0 | contract | **ControlPackAnnouncement contract fields** — A ControlPackAnnouncement carries: the artifact kind; an immutable URI and digest; version; signer/attestation; target regions/nodes; an activation window; expiry; the rollback parent; and the acknowledgments required. |  | integration: If the fetched artifact does not match the announced digest, or the signer is not trusted, the node refuses activation and sends no acknowledgment. An announcement received outside its activation window or after its expiry activates nothing. | v11.6 p39 §27 Core Contracts Between Brains — ControlPackAnnouncement |
| CONTRACT-039 | P1 | contract | **MirrorCheckpoint contract fields** — A MirrorCheckpoint carries: source and destination region; stream/partition; source epoch and offset; destination offset; lag; an integrity hash; and the time of the last successful mirror. | `MULTI_REGION` | integration: After a partition is mirrored between two regions, the checkpoint's destination offset and integrity hash match the destination's records. Once the mirror stops, the reported lag and time since the last mirror both grow. | v11.6 p39 §27 Core Contracts Between Brains — MirrorCheckpoint |
| CONTRACT-040 | P0 | invariant | **Every asynchronous event uses the one internal event model** — Every asynchronous event the platform emits travels in the one internal event model, the FabricEnvelope of CONTRACT-036, and no asynchronous path publishes a payload without it. |  | acceptance: An architecture test finds every asynchronous publication call site and asserts that each publishes through the envelope-constructing API, failing on any that sends a bare payload. | GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 3, One internal event model |
| CONTRACT-041 | P3 | capability | **fabric-client passes payloads through zero-copy buffers** — The fabric-client producer/consumer SDK is Rust-first and passes payloads through zero-copy buffers. |  | benchmark: A benchmark of produce and consume through fabric-client counts payload copies and allocations per record, and shows none between the caller's buffer and the transport. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Algorik Rust Event & Control Fabric — fabric-client row |
| CONTRACT-042 | P0 | invariant | **Producer sequence numbers make retries idempotent** — fabric-client gives each record a per-partition producer sequence number. When a record is resent with a sequence number the partition has already accepted, it is acknowledged but not appended a second time. |  | property: Under arbitrary interleavings of sends, lost acknowledgments and retries, each distinct producer sequence number appears exactly once in the partition log. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Algorik Rust Event & Control Fabric — fabric-client row ('idempotent producer sequence') |
| CONTRACT-043 | P3 | capability | **fabric-client batches records on the producer side** — fabric-client batches records asynchronously on the producer side instead of making one network write per record. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | benchmark: At a fixed record rate, the benchmark shows fewer transport writes than records and higher throughput than unbatched sends, while batching latency stays within the topic's QoS budget. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Algorik Rust Event & Control Fabric — fabric-client row ('async batching') |
| CONTRACT-044 | P0 | contract | **Every producer declares an explicit acknowledgment profile** — Every fabric-client producer declares an explicit acknowledgment profile, and no producer can be created with an implicit default. |  | unit: Constructing a producer without naming an ack profile is refused or does not compile. A send reports acknowledgment only once the declared profile's condition is met. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Algorik Rust Event & Control Fabric — fabric-client row ('explicit ack profile') |
| CONTRACT-045 | P0 | contract | **Fabric wire schema is Protobuf via prost with generated Rust types** — fabric-schema defines the Fabric wire schema in Protobuf, encoded with prost, and generates from it the Rust types that producers and consumers use. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | inspection: Every Fabric topic's payload type is generated from a registered .proto schema, and no producer or consumer hand-encodes a Fabric payload. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Algorik Rust Event & Control Fabric — fabric-schema row |
| CONTRACT-046 | P0 | invariant | **Registered schema IDs are immutable** — Once registered, a schema ID always denotes the same schema, and registering different content under an existing ID is refused. |  | unit: Re-registering an existing schema ID with different content is refused. Re-registering identical content is accepted as a no-op. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Algorik Rust Event & Control Fabric — fabric-schema row ('immutable schema IDs') |
| CONTRACT-047 | P0 | invariant | **Schema compatibility gates reject incompatible versions** — The schema registry runs a compatibility gate on every new schema version, and a version incompatible with the topic's compatibility policy is rejected before it can reach a production topic. |  | acceptance: A schema version that removes a required field (breaking backward compatibility) is rejected by both the CI check and runtime registration, and a compatible additive change is admitted. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Algorik Rust Event & Control Fabric — fabric-schema row ('compatibility gates') |
| CONTRACT-048 | P0 | contract | **Fabric frame header fields** — Every Fabric frame header contains: magic/version; message type; schema ID/version; flags; partition; producer ID/epoch; sequence; event ID; source timestamp; logical timestamp; trace ID; payload length; and a CRC32C. |  | property: For arbitrary frames, encoding and decoding round-trip every header field. Flipping any bit covered by the CRC32C is detected and refused, and a frame with a wrong magic/version or payload length is refused before its payload is read. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Frame header |
| CONTRACT-049 | P0 | invariant | **Stale producers are fenced by epoch** — A producer whose epoch is older than the current epoch registered for its producer ID is fenced, and every write it attempts after that is refused. |  | integration: Starting a second producer with the same ID bumps the epoch. The first producer's next write is refused as fenced, and none of its later records appear in the partition. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Delivery ('producer epoch/sequence prevents stale duplicate producers') |
| CONTRACT-050 | P0 | contract | **Per-partition offsets provide replay** — Each partition assigns every appended record an increasing offset, and a consumer can re-read the partition from any retained offset and receive the same records in the same order. |  | integration: Consuming a partition from offset N twice returns byte-identical records in the same order. A sink restarted from its committed offset neither skips a record nor reprocesses one it had committed. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Delivery ('per-partition offsets provide replay') |
| CONTRACT-051 | P1 | contract | **Reflex Package bundles model, strategy, feature graph, risk envelope and config** — The Reflex Package Builder bundles a compact model, a strategy, a feature graph, a risk envelope and configuration into one Reflex Package, which is delivered to regional reflex cells. |  | integration: A package built by the builder contains each of the five components, and activating a package with any component missing is refused. | diagram pL288 05 · Cognitive / AGI / Quantum Plane — Reflex Package Builder node |

| FABRIC-021 | P0 | invariant | **Each region stays independently writable; mirroring never blocks a local commit** — There must be no global or cross-region synchronous write quorum: each region's fabric must remain independently writable and operational, no local commit or acknowledgement may wait on a remote region's acknowledgement, and cross-region mirroring must be asynchronous, so that a remote-region or mirror-link outage cannot stop local execution, local journaling or control consumption. | `MULTI_REGION` | chaos: In a two-region test topology, black-hole the mirror link and then the whole remote region, and assert local produce-acknowledgement latency, local consumption and local control application are unchanged while mirror lag grows instead. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — fabric-mirror row ('No global write quorum; each region remains independently writable/operational'); v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Cross-region behavior ('A regional cluster never blocks on remote acknowledgement'); v11.6 p40 §28 Failure and Degradation Model — Cross-region fabric mirror down ('Local streams remain writable ... no cross-region synchronous quorum is attempted'); GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-mirror ('never blocks local commit'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Durability ('Cross-region mirroring is normally asynchronous'); GCP v2.1 p15 §17 Availability, Resilience and Disaster Recovery — Entire Fabric region row ('healthy regions continue'); diagram pL196-221 §03 Native Rust Event & Control Fabric — Cross-Region Mirror node ('never global synchronous quorum') |
| FABRIC-022 | P0 | contract | **Fabric contracts are versioned Protobuf schemas with immutable IDs** — Every fabric contract must be a versioned Protobuf descriptor held in the schema registry (fabric-schema) under an immutable schema ID and a schema hash, and every record on the wire must be encoded in the versioned Protobuf wire format (via prost) of the schema it names. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | unit: Registering a descriptor returns an ID and hash; re-registering identical bytes returns the same ID; any attempt to change the descriptor behind an existing ID is refused; and a record encoded under ID n decodes only with descriptor n. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — fabric-schema row ('Versioned Protobuf descriptors/contracts ... schema hashes'); v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Wire format ('versioned Protobuf via prost'); v11.6 p41 §30 Build Order — Phase 0 Foundations ('Native Rust Event & Control Fabric contracts'); GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-schema ('Protobuf/prost wire schema with immutable schema IDs'); GCP v2.1 p22 §26 Recommended Build Order — Phase 2 Rust Fabric MVP ('schemas') |
| FABRIC-023 | P0 | invariant | **CI rejects an incompatible schema change** — CI must check every fabric schema change against the backward/forward compatibility policy of the topic it serves and fail the build on an incompatible change. |  | acceptance: Submit fixture schema changes (remove a required field, renumber a field, change a field's type, add an optional field) and assert CI fails the first three and passes the fourth, proving the gate both refuses and admits. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — fabric-schema row ('compatibility checks'); GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-schema ('compatibility gates'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Schema evolution ('at CI and runtime registration') |
| FABRIC-024 | P0 | invariant | **The runtime registry refuses an incompatible schema before any production topic sees it** — The schema registry must refuse, at runtime registration, any schema incompatible with the topic's compatibility policy, and every broker must refuse a record whose schema ID is not registered and compatible for that topic, so that no incompatible schema ever reaches a production topic. |  | integration: Against a running registry and broker, register an incompatible descriptor directly (bypassing CI) and assert it is refused; then produce a record carrying an unregistered schema ID and assert the broker refuses it and no consumer receives it. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — fabric-schema row ('compatibility checks'); GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-schema ('compatibility gates'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Schema evolution ('rejected incompatible schemas never reach production topics'); diagram pL202 VIEWS.fabric — node 'f_meta' ('schemas'); diagram pL218-221 §03 Native Rust Event & Control Fabric — Meta → Broker A/B/C control edges |
| FABRIC-025 | P0 | capability | **Rust types are generated from the registered schemas** — fabric-schema must generate the Rust types producers and consumers use from the registered Protobuf descriptors, so the types in code and the descriptors in the registry cannot drift. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | acceptance: A CI check regenerates the Rust types from the registry's descriptors and fails if the result differs from the committed generated code. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — fabric-schema row ('generated Rust types'); GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-schema ('generated Rust types') |
| FABRIC-026 | P0 | contract | **Every archived segment carries a manifest, hashes, entitlements and a replay index** — Each segment fabric-archive exports must carry a manifest recording its topic, partition, offset range, content hash/checksum and entitlements, together with a replay index that locates records by offset without scanning the segment. |  | integration: Archive a segment, then verify from its manifest alone that the stored object's hash matches, the offset range is complete and contiguous with its neighbours, entitlements are present, and the replay index resolves a sampled offset to the correct record; corrupt one byte and assert verification fails. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — fabric-archive row ('manifests, hashes, entitlements and replay indexes'); GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-archive ('Closed immutable segments + manifest/checksum') |
| FABRIC-027 | P1 | capability | **Operators administer and inspect the fabric through a Rust CLI and admin API** — The fabric must provide a Rust operator CLI and internal admin API (fabricctl / fabric-inspect / fabric-admin) to create topics, set quotas and retention, and inspect stream and partition health, consumer lag, ACLs, mirroring state, replay progress and diagnostics. |  | integration: Drive every CLI command against a test cluster and assert each read reports the partition health, lag and ACLs the metadata quorum holds, and each write (topic creation, quota and retention change) is reflected in metadata and enforced by the brokers. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — fabricctl / fabric-inspect row; GCP v2.1 p8 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-admin ('Create topics, quotas, retention ... diagnostics') |
| FABRIC-028 | P0 | capability | **Operators can isolate a stream or partition in an emergency** — fabricctl must be able to isolate a stream or partition in an emergency — stopping further produce and/or consume on it without deleting it or its retained records — with the isolation recorded as an attributable operator action and reversible. |  | integration: Isolate a partition while producers and consumers are active and assert produce is refused with an isolation error, other partitions are unaffected, retained records are intact, the action is recorded with the operator identity, and lifting isolation restores service. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — fabricctl / fabric-inspect row ('emergency isolation') |
| FABRIC-029 | P0 | capability | **A latency and throughput benchmark harness runs in CI** — fabric-bench must measure fabric latency (publish-to-quorum-acknowledgement and publish-to-consume) and throughput per topic class, and must run in CI and in game days so a regression is visible before merge. |  | benchmark: The harness runs in CI against a three-broker test cluster, publishes p50/p99/p99.9 publish-to-ack and end-to-end latency and sustained throughput per class, and fails the job when a figure regresses beyond a committed threshold. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — fabric-bench / fabric-chaos row; v11.6 p41 §30 Build Order — Phase 0 Foundations ('benchmark harness') |
| FABRIC-030 | P0 | capability | **Deterministic fault and partition testing gates fabric adoption** — fabric-chaos must inject broker, zone and network-partition faults deterministically (reproducible from a seed) in CI and in game days, and application services must not adopt the fabric until its chaos suite passes. |  | chaos: Run the chaos suite twice from the same seed and assert identical fault schedules and outcomes, and assert the adoption gate blocks any application service wiring to the fabric while the suite is red. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — fabric-bench / fabric-chaos row ('deterministic fault/partition testing used in CI and game days'); GCP v2.1 p22 §26 Recommended Build Order — Phase 2 Rust Fabric MVP ('chaos tests before application adoption') |
| FABRIC-031 | P3 | nfr | **The SDK's producer and consumer APIs are zero-copy friendly** — fabric-client must offer zero-copy-friendly producer and consumer APIs over Rust-first buffers, so a record is not copied between the caller's buffer, the batch and the socket where the protocol allows. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | benchmark: Benchmark the publish and fetch paths with an allocation and copy counter and assert bytes copied per record stay within the committed budget. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — Rust SDK row ('Zero-copy-friendly producer/consumer APIs'); GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-client ('Rust-first zero-copy buffers') |
| FABRIC-032 | P0 | contract | **Idempotent producers: sequence numbers make retries duplicate-free** — Every producer must carry a producer ID and a per-partition sequence number on each record, and the broker must discard a retried record whose sequence it has already appended and refuse an out-of-sequence gap, so producer retries never create duplicates in the log. |  | property: Property test: for any interleaving of sends, lost acknowledgements and retries from one producer, the partition log contains each sequence number exactly once and in order. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — Rust SDK row ('idempotent producer sequencing'); v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Delivery ('idempotent producer IDs/sequence numbers'); GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-client ('idempotent producer sequence'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Delivery ('producer epoch/sequence prevents stale duplicate producers') |
| FABRIC-033 | P1 | capability | **Consumer groups share partitions under metadata-held leases** — fabric-client must support consumer groups: a topic's partitions are divided among a group's members under consumer leases held by fabric metadata, each partition consumed by at most one member at a time and reassigned when its owner's lease lapses. |  | property: Property test over member joins, leaves and lease expiries: at every instant each partition has at most one owner, and every partition regains an owner within one lease period after its owner leaves. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — Rust SDK row ('consumer groups'); GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-meta ('consumer leases') |
| FABRIC-034 | P1 | capability | **Consumers subscribe without polling on the caller's thread** — fabric-client must offer asynchronous (push-style) subscriptions that deliver records to a consumer as they arrive, without the caller polling in a blocking loop. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | integration: A subscriber registered on a partition receives each newly appended record within the delivery budget without issuing fetches, and a slow subscriber is paced by flow control (FABRIC-080) rather than blocking the SDK's other subscriptions. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — Rust SDK row ('async subscriptions') |
| FABRIC-035 | P0 | capability | **The SDK emits OpenTelemetry signals for every produce and consume** — fabric-client must provide OpenTelemetry hooks so every produce and consume emits metrics and carries trace context, letting a trace cross a fabric hop. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | integration: Produce and consume through the SDK with an in-memory telemetry sink and assert the produce and consume counters and latency histograms moved and the consumer's span has the producer's span as parent. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 component table — Rust SDK row ('OpenTelemetry hooks'); GCP v2.1 p22 §26 Recommended Build Order — Phase 2 Rust Fabric MVP ('OTel') |
| FABRIC-036 | P0 | contract | **Durable records use QUIC streams; datagrams only for lossy telemetry** — Durable records must travel on long-lived, reliable QUIC streams; unreliable QUIC datagrams may be used only for topic classes explicitly declared lossy telemetry. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | integration: Assert the SDK refuses to open a datagram channel for any topic whose class is not declared lossy telemetry, and that P0 to P2 records are only ever written to streams. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Transport ('long-lived streams for durable records and QUIC datagrams only for explicitly lossy telemetry classes') |
| FABRIC-037 | P0 | invariant | **Records and segments carry CRC and content-hash integrity protection** — Records and segments must carry CRC protection and BLAKE3/content hashes, verified on append, replication, fetch and archival; a broker, replica, consumer or archiver that finds a mismatch must refuse the record or segment rather than pass it on or repair it silently. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | property: Property test: flipping any single bit of a record or segment, at rest or in flight, is detected at the next verification point and the corrupted unit is refused, while unmodified units always verify. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Wire format ('BLAKE3/content hashes and CRC protection on records/segments'); diagram pL196-221 §03 Native Rust Event & Control Fabric — Segment Store node ('checksums') |
| FABRIC-038 | P0 | prohibition | **Unversioned in-memory layouts never reach the network** — Hot in-process structures may use Rust-native zero-copy layouts, but only the versioned wire format may cross the network; no unversioned memory layout may be written to a socket. |  | acceptance: An architecture test asserts every type written by the SDK's send path and the brokers' replication and mirror paths is a generated schema type encoded by the wire codec, with no raw byte reinterpretation of in-memory structs on those paths. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Wire format ('never leak unversioned memory formats onto the network') |
| FABRIC-039 | P0 | invariant | **Order is strict within a partition and never promised globally** — The fabric must deliver records in strict append order within each partition and must not promise, expose or imply a total order across partitions or regions; a consumer needing cross-partition order must derive it from record metadata (FABRIC-040). |  | property: Property test over concurrent producers and consumer restarts: each consumer observes each partition's records in exactly offset order; inspection of the SDK API finds no call that claims a cross-partition order. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Ordering ('strict per-partition order. No false promise of a total global order') |
| FABRIC-040 | P0 | contract | **Every record carries time, placement, epoch and hybrid-logical-clock metadata** — Every fabric record must carry its source event time, receive time, region, partition, leader epoch, offset and hybrid logical clock (HLC) timestamp. |  | property: Property test: every record read back from any partition has all seven fields populated, offsets are dense per partition, leader epoch never decreases along a partition, and HLC timestamps never decrease along a partition across leader changes. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Ordering ('Every record carries source event time, receive time, region, partition, leader epoch, offset and hybrid logical clock metadata'); v11.6 p38 §27 Core Contracts Between Brains — FabricEnvelope |
| FABRIC-041 | P0 | contract | **Durable streams deliver at least once; at-most-once is for telemetry only** — Delivery on every durable stream must be at-least-once to consumers by default, and at-most-once delivery may be configured only for telemetry classes. |  | property: Property test over crashes of producer, leader and consumer at arbitrary points: every quorum-acknowledged record on a durable topic is delivered to each consumer group at least once; and topic creation refuses an at-most-once profile on any non-telemetry class. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Delivery ('at-most-once allowed only for telemetry; at-least-once is default for durable streams'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Delivery ('at-least-once to consumers') |
| FABRIC-042 | P0 | contract | **Records carry deterministic event IDs and consumers deduplicate on them** — Every record must carry a deterministic event ID, stable across retries of the same source event, and consumers must deduplicate redelivered records by event ID together with partition sequence and fencing epoch. |  | property: Property test: re-producing the same source event yields the same event ID, and a consumer fed any sequence with duplicates and replays applies each event ID's effect exactly once. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Delivery ('deterministic event IDs'); GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 4 ('Consumers use event IDs, partition sequence and fencing epochs') |
| FABRIC-043 | P0 | prohibition | **No global exactly-once claim: effectively-once comes from idempotency and fencing** — Neither the fabric nor any documentation or API built on it may claim global exactly-once delivery; effectively-once processing must be achieved only as at-least-once transport plus idempotent producers, deterministic event IDs, idempotent state transitions and sinks, and fencing. |  | inspection: Inspection of the SDK, broker and sink documentation and API names finds no exactly-once delivery claim, and the effectively-once property is instead proven by the tests of FABRIC-042 and FABRIC-044. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Delivery ('provide effectively-once processing with idempotent sinks'); GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 4 ('Do not claim magical global exactly-once'); GCP v2.1 p23 §28 Explicit Anti-Patterns — 'Claiming global exactly-once delivery' |
| FABRIC-044 | P0 | invariant | **Financial outcome consumers commit each event once in effect, transactionally** — Every consumer that writes financial state — the ledger writer/sink above all — must be idempotent, enforcing uniqueness of the event ID transactionally in the same commit as the state change, so a financial outcome delivered any number of times is committed exactly once in effect. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | property: Property test: feed the ledger sink every P1 record of a session with arbitrary duplication, partition replays and crashes between the state write and the offset commit, and assert the resulting positions and cash equal those from a single clean delivery. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Delivery ('idempotent sinks'); GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 4 ('financial writers enforce uniqueness transactionally'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Delivery ('Financial consumers are idempotent'); GCP v2.1 p20 §21.1 Tick to order and learning — step 4 ('commit financial outcomes idempotently to Spanner') |
| FABRIC-045 | P0 | contract | **P0 Critical Control topics: RF3 quorum, persistent WAL, long retention and archive** — Topics of class P0 Critical Control — risk envelopes, model activation, kill/fence commands and capital grants — must acknowledge a write only after an RF3 three-zone quorum has persisted it, with control metadata and the log held in a persistent write-ahead log, and must be retained long-term with every sealed segment archived to Cloud Storage. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | chaos: Write to a P0 topic while killing one zone at random points and assert no acknowledged record is lost, no acknowledgement is issued with fewer than two replicas persisted, and every sealed segment appears in the archive. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Durability classes ('Control uses three-zone quorum plus persistent metadata/WAL'); GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 6 ('Control and outcomes get quorum durability'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P0 Critical Control row |
| FABRIC-046 | P0 | contract | **P1 Financial Outcomes topics: RF3 quorum, idempotent IDs, long hot retention and immutable archive** — Topics of class P1 Financial Outcomes — fills, cancels, position deltas and settlement events — must acknowledge only on an RF3 quorum, carry idempotent (deterministic) event IDs, keep long hot retention and archive every sealed segment immutably. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | chaos: Kill the P1 partition leader and one follower's zone during a burst of fills and assert every acknowledged fill is readable from the new leader and from the archive with its original event ID. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Durability classes ('financial outcomes use quorum replication and archival'); GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 6; GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P1 Financial Outcomes row |
| FABRIC-047 | P0 | contract | **P2 Market Journal topics: RF3 regional quorum, batch producers, tiered hot retention, GCS archive** — Topics of class P2 Market Journal — ticks, books, features and decision traces — must replicate on an RF3 regional quorum with batching producers as high-throughput replicated segments, keep hours to days of hot retention set by instrument tier, and archive sealed segments to Cloud Storage. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | integration: Publish a recorded tick session through batching producers and assert each instrument tier's hot window matches its declared retention, older segments are present only in the archive, and a replay from archive plus hot log reproduces the session. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Durability classes ('market journals use high-throughput replicated segments'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P2 Market Journal row |
| FABRIC-048 | P0 | contract | **P4 Telemetry topics: best effort or RF2, sampled or dropped oldest-first under pressure** — Topics of class P4 Telemetry — metrics-derived events and debug traces — may be acknowledged best-effort or on RF2, and under pressure must be sampled or drop their oldest records first, with every drop counted. |  | integration: Saturate a broker with P4 traffic beyond its quota and assert P4 records are sampled or dropped oldest-first, the drops are counted, and no P0 to P2 record on the same broker is delayed beyond its budget. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Durability classes ('telemetry can be sampled/dropped under pressure'); GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 6 ('telemetry can be sampled/dropped'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P4 Telemetry row |
| FABRIC-049 | P0 | nfr | **Every stream has explicit byte and message quotas, lag limits and an overload policy** — Every stream must be configured with explicit byte and message quotas (including per-producer quotas), consumer lag limits and a declared overload policy, and the brokers must enforce them. |  | integration: Exceed a producer's byte quota, then its message quota, and let a consumer fall past its lag limit, and assert each triggers the stream's declared overload action, is counted, and leaves other streams unaffected. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Backpressure ('every stream has explicit byte/message quotas, lag limits and overload policy'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Backpressure ('per-producer quotas') |
| FABRIC-050 | P0 | prohibition | **Critical control and outcome records are never silently dropped** — Under backpressure or overload, P0 control and P1 outcome records must never be silently dropped: when the fabric cannot accept one, the producer must receive an explicit refusal it can act on, and nothing already acknowledged may be discarded. |  | chaos: Drive a broker into overload with mixed traffic and, by reconciling producer-side send logs against the partitions, assert every P0 and P1 send either appears in the log or received an explicit refusal — none vanished. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Backpressure ('Critical control/outcomes cannot be silently dropped'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P0 Critical Control row ('never intentionally dropped') |
| FABRIC-051 | P0 | invariant | **Telemetry and ambient signals are shed before control or outcomes are starved** — Topic priority must order shedding: under pressure, P4 telemetry and low-value ambient signals must be sampled or shed before any P0 control or P1 outcome traffic is delayed or starved. |  | chaos: Freeze a sink and flood P3 and P4 topics (v2.1 §25's broker-backpressure game day, G p22) and assert P0 and P1 publish-to-acknowledgement latency stays within budget while P4 sampling engages first. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Backpressure ('telemetry and low-value ambient signals can be sampled or shed'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Backpressure ('Low-priority telemetry is sampled/dropped before control/outcome traffic is starved') |
| FABRIC-052 | P1 | placement | **Cross-region mirror traffic stays on private networking** — Cross-region mirror traffic must travel only over Google private networking, with the mirror prefixes explicitly exported through the latency NCC hub and no other cross-region route. | `MULTI_REGION` `MANAGED_SERVICE` | infra-plan: terraform plan shows the mirror prefixes as the only fabric prefixes exported to the latency NCC hub, and no public route or external IP on any mirror endpoint. | v11.6 p36 §26.1 Protocol and semantics — Cross-region behavior ('over Google private networking'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — IP identity ('Cross-region mirror prefixes are explicitly exported through the latency NCC hub') |
| FABRIC-053 | P0 | prohibition | **The fabric carries package announcements, never the packages** — For model and policy packages the fabric must carry only version, digest, availability and activation messages; the packages themselves must be stored as immutable signed artifacts in object/artifact storage and never carried on the fabric. |  | acceptance: An acceptance test asserts every schema registered for a package topic holds only version, digest, availability and activation fields within a bounded record size, and a node activates a package only after fetching the artifact from storage and verifying its digest and signature. | v11.6 p36-37 §26.1 Hot-path contract — 'the fabric carries only version/digest/availability/activation messages' |
| FABRIC-054 | P0 | failure_behavior | **When the fabric is unavailable a node runs on its last valid package within a bounded local journal** — If its regional fabric is unavailable (including loss of quorum or of the whole regional fabric), a Reflex Node must continue under its last valid cached signed control package and its local journal, stop accepting new control changes, queue durable publications locally within a bounded disk budget, and degrade as policy defines before the journal is exhausted and no later than the package's TTL or the point its risk policy requires. |  | chaos: Cut a paper Reflex cell off from its fabric and assert it keeps deciding under its cached package, journals locally, refuses new control, degrades on the configured trigger before its journal budget is reached and halts new exposure at package TTL; restore the fabric and assert the spool drains in order with no duplicates. | v11.6 p36-37 §26.1 Hot-path contract — 'a node continues under its last valid package and local journal until the package TTL or risk policy requires degradation'; v11.6 p40 §28 Failure and Degradation Model — Regional Event Fabric quorum lost row; v11.6 p44 §31 Capability Completeness Checklist — 'cached signed control packages'; GCP v2.1 p15 §17 Availability, Resilience and Disaster Recovery — Entire Fabric region row ('Reflex can continue under cached policy') |
| FABRIC-055 | P0 | failure_behavior | **Broker loss moves leadership to an in-sync follower; producers and consumers carry on** — On the loss of a broker, leadership of each partition it led must move to an in-sync follower in another zone; producers must refresh the partition map from metadata and retry by producer epoch, consumers must resume from their committed offsets, and Reflex execution must not wait for the failover. |  | chaos: Kill a broker leading partitions of every class during steady produce and consume and assert new leaders are in-sync followers in other zones, producers resume after refreshing the map with no duplicates and no loss of acknowledged records, and consumers continue from committed offsets. | v11.6 p40 §28 Failure and Degradation Model — Regional Event Fabric broker loss row; GCP v2.1 p15 §17 Availability, Resilience and Disaster Recovery — Fabric broker row |
| FABRIC-056 | P1 | nfr | **Mirror lag has an independent, visible, bounded budget** — Each cross-region mirror must run to its own lag budget — its lag never back-pressures local commit or other mirrors — and its lag must be measured, visible and bounded, with a breach of the budget raised rather than absorbed. | `MULTI_REGION` | chaos: Throttle one mirror link and assert its lag metric rises and trips its budget alarm while local commit latency and the other mirror's lag are unchanged. | v11.6 p40 §28 Failure and Degradation Model — Cross-region fabric mirror down row ('Mirror lag is visible and bounded'); GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-mirror ('independent lag budget') |
| FABRIC-057 | P0 | invariant | **Every stream declares its class and semantics; nothing rests on broker defaults** — Every durable stream must be created with an explicit QoS class (P0 to P4) and declared partitioning key, ordering, retention, replication, overload and mirroring semantics, and the fabric must refuse to create a stream that leaves any of them to an unspecified broker default; durability is set per topic by its class, never globally. |  | unit: Topic creation with any of the seven declarations missing is refused with an error naming the missing one; with all present it succeeds and the stored definition round-trips every declared value. | v11.6 p44 §31 Capability Completeness Checklist — 'Every durable event stream declares partitioning, ordering, retention, replication, overload and mirroring semantics'; GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 6 ('Durability is per topic'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes |
| FABRIC-058 | P0 | invariant | **Producer fencing: a stale producer epoch is refused** — Fabric metadata must assign each producer an epoch, and every broker must refuse writes from a producer whose epoch is older than the current one for its producer ID, so a zombie or superseded producer cannot append after its successor has started; P0 control topics must require producer fencing. |  | property: Property test: for any schedule in which producer instance A is superseded by B for the same producer ID, including A resuming after a pause, no record from A under the old epoch is appended after B's first append. | GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 4 ('fencing epochs'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Delivery ('producer epoch/sequence prevents stale duplicate producers'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P0 Critical Control row ('producer fencing'); GCP v2.1 p23 §28 Explicit Anti-Patterns — 'idempotent state transitions and fencing'; diagram pL202 VIEWS.fabric — node 'f_meta' ('producer fencing'); diagram pL218-221 §03 Native Rust Event & Control Fabric — Meta → Broker A/B/C control edges |
| FABRIC-059 | P1 | contract | **P3 Intelligence/Research topics: configurable RF2/3, throughput batching, replayable backlog** — Topics of class P3 Intelligence/Research — evidence deltas, episodes and training candidates — must be replicated RF2 or RF3 by configuration, batched for throughput, replayable, allowed to accumulate backlog within their declared retention rather than shed, and served by consumers that scale out. |  | integration: Stall P3 consumers for a sustained interval and assert no P3 record is shed, the backlog stays within the topic's retention, and adding consumers drains it. | GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 6 ('research streams optimize throughput'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P3 Intelligence/Research row |
| FABRIC-060 | P0 | placement | **Each region's fabric lives in its own project: VPC, broker VMs, journal disks, archiver identities** — Each region's fabric must be provisioned in a dedicated prod/fabric-<region> project holding the fabric VPC, broker VMs, journal disks and archiver service identities, separate from the execution (Reflex) and services projects, so that a messaging failure or misconfiguration cannot directly reconfigure trading compute. |  | infra-plan: terraform plan shows one fabric project per region containing the fabric VPC, broker VMs, journal disks and archiver identities, and no IAM grant giving a fabric identity any role on that region's execution project. | GCP v2.1 p4 §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model — prod/fabric-<region> row |
| FABRIC-061 | P0 | prohibition | **The fabric implements only the semantics the platform needs, each proven by fault or property tests** — The fabric must implement only the semantics the platform requires — it is not a feature-for-feature Kafka clone — and each semantic guarantee it offers must be proven by a fault-injection or property test before anything relies on it. |  | inspection: Inspection maps every guarantee in the fabric's specification (ordering, delivery, durability per class, fencing, backpressure, mirroring) to at least one named property or chaos test that has been mutation-verified; a guarantee without one fails review. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Algorik Rust Event & Control Fabric — introduction ('not a clone of Kafka feature-for-feature. It implements only the semantics the platform needs'); GCP v2.1 p23 §28 Explicit Anti-Patterns — 'Rebuilding Kafka semantics blindly' |
| FABRIC-062 | P0 | nfr | **fabricd is directed onto the Tokio async runtime** — fabricd must be built on an async runtime, which v2.1's implementation direction names as Tokio. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | inspection: Inspection of the dependency record admitting an async runtime and of fabricd's crate: the runtime is the recorded one and no other executor is present. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabricd ('Tokio async runtime') |
| FABRIC-063 | P0 | invariant | **Broker memory is bounded: pooled buffers and bounded queues** — fabricd must allocate from bounded memory pools and hold every in-flight queue to a fixed bound, so overload produces backpressure or refusal rather than unbounded memory growth. |  | chaos: Freeze a sink and fill consumer lag (v2.1 §25's broker-backpressure game day, G p22) and assert broker resident memory stays under its configured ceiling throughout. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabricd ('bounded memory pools'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Backpressure ('bounded queues') |
| FABRIC-064 | P3 | nfr | **Journal I/O mode is chosen by benchmark** — Whether fabricd uses direct or buffered I/O for its journal must be decided by benchmark on the target disks, with the choice and its measurement recorded. |  | benchmark: fabric-bench runs append and fetch workloads under both I/O modes on the target disk type, and the recorded choice matches the better measured p99 at the required throughput. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabricd ('direct/buffered I/O chosen by benchmark') |
| FABRIC-065 | P0 | invariant | **Metadata is kept separate from the data log** — Fabric metadata (membership, partition maps, epochs, leases, quotas, ACLs) must live in the metadata quorum's own replicated log, separate from partition data logs. |  | integration: With a data partition's disk full, assert metadata operations (leader election, ACL change) still commit; and inspection shows no metadata record type in any partition log. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-meta ('metadata separated from data log') |
| FABRIC-066 | P1 | capability | **Producers batch records for throughput** — fabric-client must batch records per partition in the background of the caller, within a bounded batch size and a bounded linger time. |  | benchmark: A throughput benchmark shows batched produce reaching the P2 class's target rate, and a test asserts no batch exceeds its size bound or lingers past its time bound. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-client ('async batching') |
| FABRIC-067 | P0 | contract | **Producers choose an explicit acknowledgement profile no weaker than their topic's class** — Every produce must use an explicit acknowledgement profile (for example quorum, leader-only or none), and the SDK must refuse a profile weaker than the topic class's declared durability requires. |  | unit: For each class, the SDK accepts the profile the class requires and refuses every weaker one (for example leader-only on P0) with an error naming the class. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-client ('explicit ack profile') |
| FABRIC-068 | P0 | capability | **Replay can hydrate from the GCS archive** — Replay must be able to hydrate partitions and read records from archived segments in Cloud Storage, through their manifests and replay indexes, once those segments are no longer on any broker. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | replay: Let a partition's early segments age out of broker retention, replay the partition from offset zero, and assert the archived portion is read from the archive and the combined stream equals the original. | GCP v2.1 p7 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-archive ('replay can hydrate from GCS') |
| FABRIC-069 | P0 | invariant | **Sinks isolate destination backpressure from the brokers** — Fabric sinks (fabric-sink-* for Bigtable, BigQuery, Spanner and GCS) must run as consumers outside the brokers, so a slow or failed destination backs up only that sink's consumer lag and never slows broker ingest or other consumers. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | chaos: Freeze each destination fake in turn and assert broker append latency and other consumers' throughput are unchanged while only the frozen sink's lag grows (v2.1 §25 broker-backpressure game day). | GCP v2.1 p8 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-sink-* ('Isolate destination backpressure from brokers') |
| FABRIC-070 | P1 | capability | **Admin tooling moves partitions, drains leadership, repairs and compacts** — The fabric's admin/repair/rebalance component must be able, on every broker, to move partitions, drain leadership from a broker, enforce retention, repair under-replicated partitions and perform offline compaction. |  | integration: Under live traffic, move a partition between brokers, drain a broker's leadership and repair a partition with a missing replica, and assert after each that no acknowledged record is lost, RF3 is restored and consumers see no gap. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-admin ('partition moves, drain'); diagram pL208 VIEWS.fabric — 03 · Native Rust Event & Control Fabric, node 'f_admin' ('Partition moves, retention, repair, offline compaction'); diagram pL218-221 §03 Native Rust Event & Control Fabric — Admin → Broker A/B/C control edges |
| FABRIC-071 | P0 | invariant | **Admin access requires mutual TLS and an IAM-bound identity** — Every fabric admin API or CLI call must be authenticated with mutual TLS and authorised against an IAM-bound workload or operator identity, and must be refused otherwise. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` `MANAGED_SERVICE` | integration: Call each admin operation without a client certificate, with a valid certificate but an identity lacking the IAM binding, and with a bound identity, and assert only the last succeeds and every attempt is audited. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-admin ('mTLS and IAM-bound access') |
| FABRIC-072 | P0 | capability | **The fabric exports native OpenTelemetry metrics, traces and health** — fabric-observe must export broker, metadata and mirror metrics, traces and health natively in OpenTelemetry form, each metric recorded at the seam where its fact becomes known. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | integration: Run a test cluster with an in-memory telemetry receiver and assert every documented fabric metric has at least one data point after a produce/consume/failover cycle, recorded by a non-test caller. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-observe ('Native OTel metrics'); GCP v2.1 p22 §26 Recommended Build Order — Phase 2 Rust Fabric MVP ('OTel') |
| FABRIC-073 | P0 | invariant | **Fabric health never depends on the fabric's own topics** — Fabric liveness and health must be observable through direct OpenTelemetry export and health endpoints and must not rely on the fabric's own event topics; the P4 Telemetry class is never the primary health path. |  | chaos: Stop every broker in a test cluster and assert the fabric's health endpoints and telemetry exporter still report the outage. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7 Rust Fabric component rows — fabric-observe ('does not rely on its own event topics for liveness'); GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P4 Telemetry row ('direct OTel remains primary health path') |
| FABRIC-074 | P3 | nfr | **Bulk mirror transport is chosen by benchmark, TCP included** — For specific long-lived bulk mirror flows, TCP must be benchmarked against QUIC and the transport chosen by measurement rather than by assuming one protocol wins everywhere; mutual TLS is required either way. |  | benchmark: fabric-bench compares mutually authenticated QUIC and TCP on a representative cross-region bulk mirror flow, and the recorded choice matches the measured throughput and tail latency. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Transport ('Benchmark TCP for specific long-lived bulk mirror flows') |
| FABRIC-075 | P0 | contract | **Partitions are chosen by an explicit ordering key** — Every produce must name an explicit ordering key, and all records with the same key on a topic must land in the same partition. |  | property: Property test: for any set of keys and any sequence of produces, all records sharing a key sit in one partition and appear in produce order. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Partitioning ('explicit ordering key') |
| FABRIC-076 | P1 | contract | **Partition leaders are placed by rendezvous or consistent assignment** — Partition leadership must be assigned to brokers by rendezvous or consistent-hash assignment, so adding or removing a broker moves only the partitions that must move. |  | property: Property test: adding one broker to an n-broker cluster moves roughly 1/(n+1) of leaderships, and no leadership moves between two brokers present both before and after. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Partitioning ('rendezvous/consistent assignment to partition leaders') |
| FABRIC-077 | P0 | invariant | **A quorum ack means a majority persisted it, and no quorum-acked record is lost to a broker or zone failure** — A quorum acknowledgement must be issued only after a majority of the partition's RF3 replicas has persisted the record, so that a single broker or a whole zone can fail without losing any quorum-acknowledged P0, P1 or P2 record. |  | chaos: On a three-zone cluster under random broker kills, zone partitions and restarts, record every acknowledged write and assert after healing that each is present in its partition, in order, on the current leader. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Durability ('A quorum acknowledgment means the record survived on a majority of replicas'); GCP v2.1 p15 §17 Availability, Resilience and Disaster Recovery — Fabric broker row ('Quorum-acked records preserved'); GCP v2.1 p23 §27 Architecture Acceptance Criteria — 'A Fabric broker/zone can fail without losing quorum-acknowledged P0/P1/P2 records' |
| FABRIC-078 | P0 | invariant | **Append batches are atomic within one partition** — A batch appended to one partition must become visible atomically: consumers see all of its records or none, never a prefix. |  | property: Property test: crash the leader at arbitrary points during batch appends and assert no consumer ever observes a strict prefix of a batch. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Atomicity ('atomic append batches within one partition') |
| FABRIC-079 | P0 | prohibition | **Cross-partition business transactions are sagas, not broker transactions** — A business transaction spanning partitions must be represented as an explicit saga of commands and compensations recorded as ordinary records; the fabric must not offer, and nothing may rely on, hidden cross-partition broker transactions. |  | inspection: Inspection of the fabric API finds no multi-partition transaction primitive, and each cross-partition flow in the platform has a documented saga with a replay test of its compensation path. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Atomicity ('Cross-partition business transactions are represented as sagas/commands, not hidden broker transactions') |
| FABRIC-080 | P0 | nfr | **Credit/window flow control paces every session** — The fabric must use credit/window flow control on every session, so a sender transmits only within credit its receiver has granted. |  | integration: Stop a consumer from granting credit and assert the broker sends nothing beyond the outstanding window; likewise a producer beyond its window is paused rather than buffered without bound. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.1 Wire, ordering and delivery semantics — Backpressure ('credit/window flow control') |
| FABRIC-081 | P0 | invariant | **P0 control payloads are signed and verified before they are acted on** — Every P0 Critical Control payload must be signed by its authorised producer, and every consumer must verify the signature against the expected signer before acting on it, refusing an unsigned or badly signed record. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | integration: Deliver a validly signed, an unsigned and a wrongly signed risk envelope to a paper Reflex cell and assert only the first is applied and the other two are refused and journaled. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P0 Critical Control row ('signed payload') |
| FABRIC-082 | P0 | invariant | **The ledger sink retries indefinitely and never drops a financial outcome** — The ledger sink consuming P1 Financial Outcomes must retry a failed commit indefinitely with backoff, never skipping or dropping the record, and must not advance its offset past a record until that record is committed; its retries and lag must be observable. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | chaos: Deny writes to the ledger store for a sustained interval and assert the sink's committed offset does not advance, no P1 record is skipped, the retry and lag metrics move, and on restore every outcome commits once in effect (v2.1 §25 ledger-outage game day). | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P1 Financial Outcomes row ('ledger sink retries indefinitely') |
| FABRIC-083 | P1 | invariant | **Market-journal mirroring is throttled before local ingest** — Under pressure, mirroring of P2 Market Journal topics must be throttled before local P2 ingest is slowed. |  | chaos: Saturate a broker with P2 ingest while mirroring and assert mirror throughput drops first and local append latency stays within budget. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.2 Fabric topic classes — P2 Market Journal row ('throttles mirror before local ingest') |
| FABRIC-084 | P1 | placement | **Production regions start with five broker VMs across three zones** — Each production region must initially run five C4D/C4-class broker VMs spread across three zones; three is the minimum, and five provides maintenance headroom and reduces correlated quorum pressure. | `COST` `MULTI_REGION` | infra-plan: terraform plan for a production region declares five C4D/C4-family broker instances across three zones, and a plan with fewer than three is refused by variable validation (the gate proven to refuse a bad value and admit a good one). | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — Brokers ('five C4D/C4 VM instances per production region initially') |
| FABRIC-085 | P1 | placement | **Broker journals live on persistent Hyperdisk, with local SSD only as cache** — Broker journal disks must be persistent Hyperdisk sized for sustained append and read throughput; local SSD and page cache may be used only for transient acceleration. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` `COST` | infra-plan: terraform plan attaches Hyperdisk journal volumes whose provisioned throughput meets the P2 class's sustained rate to every broker, and mounts any local SSD only as cache. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — Journal disks |
| FABRIC-086 | P0 | invariant | **Journal durability derives from replication, never from one device** — No durability guarantee may depend on a single local device: a record counts as durable only when replicated as its class requires (FABRIC-077), and the loss of any one broker's disk must lose no acknowledged record. |  | chaos: Destroy one broker's journal disk and its local cache under load and assert every acknowledged record remains readable and the broker is rebuilt from replicas. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — Journal disks ('Durability derives from replicated journal, not one local device') |
| FABRIC-087 | P1 | placement | **Clients bootstrap from Cloud DNS SRV records** — Fabric clients must find bootstrap broker endpoints through Cloud DNS SRV records, optionally backed by Service Directory. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | infra-plan: terraform plan declares a private Cloud DNS zone with SRV records for each region's fabric bootstrap endpoints, and a client configured only with the SRV name connects. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — Discovery ('Cloud DNS SRV records and optionally Service Directory provide bootstrap endpoints') |
| FABRIC-088 | P0 | contract | **Clients take the live broker and partition map from fabric metadata** — After bootstrap, clients must obtain the live broker/partition map from fabric metadata, not from DNS, and must send each partition's records to that partition's current leader, refreshing the map when leadership changes; a Reflex Node therefore holds a session to every broker that leads one of its partitions. |  | integration: Move a partition's leadership while a producer is active and assert the producer's next send goes to the new leader after a map refresh, with no DNS change, and that no record is sent to a follower. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — Discovery ('clients obtain the live broker/partition map from Fabric metadata'); diagram pL178-184 §02 Regional Cell — algorik-node → Broker A, B and C data edges |
| FABRIC-089 | P0 | invariant | **Brokers have stable internal addresses and no public endpoint** — Every broker must have a stable internal address and no public endpoint or external IP. |  | infra-plan: terraform plan shows a static internal address on every broker and no external IP, public load balancer or firewall rule admitting 0.0.0.0/0 to any broker port. | GCP v2.1 p8 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — IP identity ('stable internal addresses, no public broker endpoints') |
| FABRIC-090 | P0 | invariant | **Archived segments are content-addressed in regional landing buckets** — Each closed segment must be written to its region's Cloud Storage landing bucket under a content address (its hash), so an archived object's name proves its content. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | integration: Archive segments to a landing-bucket fake and assert every object name equals the hash of its bytes, re-archiving the same segment is a no-op, and a tampered object fails the name check. | GCP v2.1 p9 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — Archival ('closed segments are content-addressed and written to regional GCS landing buckets') |
| FABRIC-091 | P1 | process | **Archived segments move to research/archive locations only as residency policy allows** — Segments must be lifecycled or copied from regional landing buckets to durable research/archive locations only as the applicable data-residency policy allows. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | infra-plan: terraform plan shows lifecycle and copy rules from each landing bucket only to locations the residency policy permits for that region, and a fixture policy forbidding a destination removes that rule. | GCP v2.1 p9 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — Archival ('lifecycle/copied to durable research/archive locations according to residency policy') |
| FABRIC-092 | P1 | process | **Brokers are scaled deliberately, partitions ahead of peak — never by reactive autoscaling** — Fabric capacity must be scaled by adding brokers and rebalancing leaders and followers, and by increasing partitions per domain ahead of expected peaks; brokers must not be autoscaled reactively like stateless pods. | `COST` | infra-plan: terraform plan attaches no autoscaler to the broker instance group, and a rebalance drill adding one broker moves leaderships with no loss of acknowledged records. | GCP v2.1 p9 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — Scaling; GCP v2.1 p16 §18 Scaling and Performance Model — Fabric row ('Add brokers, move leaders/followers, increase partitions by domain') |
| FABRIC-093 | P1 | process | **Brokers are upgraded one at a time: drain, verify, replace, rejoin, advance** — Broker upgrades must proceed one broker at a time: drain its leadership, verify replica health, replace its immutable image or binary, let it rejoin, and only then advance to the next. |  | integration: Rolling-upgrade a three-zone test cluster under live traffic and assert no two brokers are ever out of service together, replica health is verified before each advance, and no acknowledged record is lost. | GCP v2.1 p9 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — Upgrade |
| FABRIC-094 | P0 | prohibition | **An upgrade never takes enough replicas down to lose quorum** — No upgrade or maintenance action may take down, at the same time, enough replicas of any partition or of the metadata quorum to lose quorum, and a rollout must refuse to advance while any partition is under-replicated. |  | property: With one partition under-replicated, attempt to advance the rollout and assert it refuses; a property test over rollout schedules asserts no schedule the controller accepts ever leaves a partition or the metadata quorum below quorum. | GCP v2.1 p9 §7.3 Fabric placement on GCP — Upgrade ('Never upgrade enough replicas simultaneously to lose quorum') |
| FABRIC-095 | P1 | placement | **Fabric consumers and sinks run on dedicated node pools** — Fabric consumers and sink workers must run on dedicated GKE node pools that no other warm service shares. | `KUBERNETES` | infra-plan: terraform plan and the workload manifests place every sink and consumer on a dedicated, tainted node pool that no other workload tolerates. | GCP v2.1 p9 §8 Regional GKE Service Plane — Fabric consumers/sinks row ('Dedicated node pools') |
| FABRIC-096 | P1 | nfr | **Sink and consumer capacity scales on consumer lag** — Fabric consumer and sink capacity must scale on consumer lag, up to the partition count, rather than on CPU alone. | `KUBERNETES` | integration: Grow a sink's lag past its scaling threshold and assert the autoscaler adds consumers up to the partition count and removes them once lag drains. | GCP v2.1 p9 §8 Regional GKE Service Plane — Fabric consumers/sinks row ('Scale from consumer lag') |
| FABRIC-097 | P1 | nfr | **Each sink's failure and backpressure are isolated from the others** — Each sink (Spanner, Bigtable, BigQuery, GCS) must have its own consumer, backpressure and failure isolation, so one slow or failing destination cannot stall any other sink. |  | chaos: Freeze the BigQuery destination fake and assert the Spanner, Bigtable and GCS sinks keep their throughput and lag unchanged. | GCP v2.1 p9 §8 Regional GKE Service Plane — Fabric consumers/sinks row ('destination-specific failure isolation'); diagram pL172 VIEWS.regional — 02 · Regional Cell, node 'sink' ('Spanner/Bigtable/BQ/GCS sinks with independent backpressure') |
| FABRIC-098 | P1 | failure_behavior | **A lost broker is replaced and partitions rebalanced back to full replication** — After a broker failure, the broker must be replaced from its immutable image and partitions rebalanced so that every durable partition returns to RF3 across three zones without data loss. |  | chaos: Kill a broker permanently, run the replacement procedure, and assert every durable partition returns to three in-sync replicas across three zones with no loss of acknowledged records. | GCP v2.1 p15 §17 Availability, Resilience and Disaster Recovery — Fabric broker row (recovery: 'replace broker and rebalance') |
| FABRIC-099 | P1 | failure_behavior | **Critical mirrored topics stay readable elsewhere when a region's fabric is lost** — When an entire regional fabric is lost, its critical mirrored topics (control and outcomes) must remain readable in other regions, up to the mirror lag at the moment of loss. | `MULTI_REGION` | game-day: Remove one region's fabric in a multi-region staging game day and assert its mirrored P0 and P1 topics are readable in each surviving region up to the recorded mirror lag. | GCP v2.1 p15 §17 Availability, Resilience and Disaster Recovery — Entire Fabric region row ('critical mirrored topics available elsewhere') |
| FABRIC-100 | P1 | failure_behavior | **A lost regional fabric is rebuilt from surviving replicas and GCS archives** — A lost regional fabric must be rebuildable from surviving replicas and its Cloud Storage segment archive while healthy regions continue. | `MULTI_REGION` | game-day: Rebuild a nonprod regional fabric from zero using only Terraform, surviving replicas and its archive (v2.1 §25's rebuild-from-zero drill, G p22) and assert every archived offset range is present and consumers resume. | GCP v2.1 p15 §17 Availability, Resilience and Disaster Recovery — Entire Fabric region row (recovery: 'Bring region back from surviving replicas/GCS archives') |
| FABRIC-101 | P1 | nfr | **Fabric keeps capacity headroom for a zone loss and for maintenance** — Fabric capacity must keep enough headroom to absorb the loss of one zone and a broker under maintenance at peak load. | `COST` | benchmark: With one zone's brokers removed and one further broker drained, fabric-bench at the recorded peak rate keeps every class within its latency budget. | GCP v2.1 p16 §18 Scaling and Performance Model — Fabric row ('keep headroom for zone loss and maintenance') |
| FABRIC-102 | P1 | prohibition | **Eventarc is not part of core internal eventing** — Eventarc must not be used for core internal eventing; it may be used only for peripheral Google-service automation that does not become an application dependency. |  | acceptance: An architecture test fails if any workspace service is the target of an Eventarc trigger, and inspection of Terraform finds Eventarc triggers only on peripheral automation targets. | GCP v2.1 p18 §19.1 Deliberately not used as core internal messaging — Eventarc row |
| FABRIC-103 | P1 | prohibition | **Cloud Tasks is not an internal general queue** — Cloud Tasks must not be used as an internal general-purpose queue; it may be used only by isolated customer-facing workflows whose task semantics specifically fit. |  | acceptance: An architecture test fails if any internal service enqueues to, or is invoked by, Cloud Tasks outside an allow-list of isolated customer-facing workflows. | GCP v2.1 p18 §19.1 Deliberately not used as core internal messaging — Cloud Tasks row |
| FABRIC-104 | P1 | contract | **Regional warm services publish policy, envelopes, grants and research events to the fabric** — Regional warm (GKE) services must publish policy, risk-envelope and capital-grant events as P0 control, the financial outcome events they originate (such as settlement events) as P1, and research, world and knowledge events as P3, to their regional fabric asynchronously. | `KUBERNETES` | integration: Run the capital and risk services against a test fabric and assert each envelope and grant appears on a P0 topic and each research event on a P3 topic, and that no publish blocks the service's request path. | GCP v2.1 p19 §20 Critical Service-to-Service Connection Matrix — GKE control service → Regional Fabric row ('Publish policy, research, capital/risk envelope events'); diagram pL196-221 §03 Native Rust Event & Control Fabric — GKE Services node ('P0/P1/P3: Risk envelopes, capital grants, world/knowledge events') and control edge |
| FABRIC-105 | P1 | contract | **Regional warm services consume ordered partitions from the fabric in consumer groups** — Regional warm services — Risk Brain, Capital/Treasury, Asset/Strategy, Evidence/World Model, Ambient/Causal agents and the sink workers — must consume the fabric's ordered partitions by asynchronous pull/stream in consumer groups, with replay. | `KUBERNETES` | integration: Run two instances of the risk service in one consumer group against a test fabric and assert each partition is consumed by one instance in offset order, and that restarting one instance resumes from its committed offsets. | GCP v2.1 p19 §20 Critical Service-to-Service Connection Matrix — Regional Fabric → GKE consumers row; diagram pL128-138 §01 Global Platform Topology — Regional Fabric → Regional GKE edges; diagram pL178-184 §02 Regional Cell — Broker A → Risk Brain, Capital/Treasury, Asset/Strategy, Evidence/World Model, Ambient/Causal Agents and Fabric Sink Workers edges; diagram pL218-221 §03 Native Rust Event & Control Fabric — Broker A → Regional GKE Consumers edge |

Reflex Mesh and multi-leg arbitrage coordination.

| MESH-001 | P1 | capability | **Regional Reflex nodes coordinate multi-leg opportunities with their peers over the Reflex Mesh** — Regional Reflex nodes exchange latency-sensitive state directly with peer regional nodes, and coordinate distributed multi-leg opportunities of 2 to 20 legs (MESH-010) over the Reflex Mesh (peer reflex messaging). That coordination is not routed through the global brain. | `MULTI_REGION` `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | integration: Two paper Reflex cells in different regions, connected only by the peer mesh and with the global brain unreachable, exchange edge state and carry a 2-leg cross-region paper cycle from opportunity token to completion. | EXEC-008 | P2 | capability | **The Market Factory seeds initial liquidity in a created market** — When the Market Factory creates a market, it must be able to seed initial liquidity in it and so bootstrap liquidity in the new market. | `LIVE_CAPITAL` `EXTERNAL_ACTION` | integration: In simulation, a created market receives the Factory's seed orders within their approved size. | EXEC-034 | P1 | nfr | **Each venue has its own connection pool** — The Reflex node must keep a separate connection pool for each venue's sessions. |  | chaos: With two simulated venues, repeated forced disconnects at one venue leave the other venue's session count and order latency unchanged. | GCP v2.1 p6 §6 Regional Reflex Cell - Speed-Critical Execution — Venue sessions bullet ('per-venue connection pools') |
