## RISK

Risk Brain and deterministic Risk Gate.

| ID | P | Kind | Requirement | Flags | Verification | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RISK-001 | P0 | invariant | **Money movement bounded by a deterministic control** — Every movement of money (a transfer, conversion, funding or withdrawal between accounts, venues, custodians or regions) is bounded by a deterministic, testable control, and that bound holds however the movement was originated, including by AI acting automatically inside its pre-authorised envelope. |  | property: For generated transfer requests from every originating component, model-originated ones included, a request exceeding its corridor or cap is refused, the same request against the same state always gets the same verdict, and a mutation that removes the cap makes the test fail. | v11.6 p4 §1.2 Non-Negotiable Safety/Correctness Boundary |
| RISK-002 | P0 | invariant | **Leverage bounded by a deterministic limit** — Leverage is bounded by a deterministic, testable limit that is checked before an order or position change exists, whatever originated the action. |  | property: For generated books and orders, an order whose fill would take leverage over the limit is refused before an order object exists, one that stays under it is admitted, the verdict is identical on re-evaluation, and a mutation that disables the limit makes the test fail. | v11.6 p4 §1.2 Non-Negotiable Safety/Correctness Boundary |
| RISK-003 | P0 | invariant | **Exposure bounded by deterministic limits** — Exposure is bounded by deterministic, testable limits that are checked before an order exists, whatever originated the action. |  | property: For generated books and orders, an order that would take exposure past any configured exposure limit is refused before an order object exists, an order inside every limit is admitted, and a mutation that disables any single limit makes a test fail. | v11.6 p4 §1.2 Non-Negotiable Safety/Correctness Boundary |
| RISK-004 | P0 | invariant | **Settlement exposure bounded by a deterministic limit** — Settlement exposure (value committed to trades or transfers that have not yet settled) is bounded by a deterministic, testable limit. |  | property: For generated sequences of trades and settlements, an action that would take unsettled value past the limit is refused, capacity is released only when the ledger records settlement, and a mutation that ignores unsettled legs makes the test fail. | v11.6 p4 §1.2 Non-Negotiable Safety/Correctness Boundary |
| RISK-005 | P0 | invariant | **Venue access bounded by a deterministic control** — Access to a venue is bounded by a deterministic, testable control. An action bound for a venue that the operating policy does not permit is refused before it reaches the venue adapter. |  | acceptance: An action addressed to a venue outside the permitted set, a live-class venue included, is refused before any adapter is called and the refusal is recorded. The same action addressed to a permitted simulated venue is admitted, which proves the control is not refusing everything. | v11.6 p4 §1.2 Non-Negotiable Safety/Correctness Boundary |
| RISK-006 | P0 | invariant | **Every executable action passes pre-trade limits** — Every executable action passes the deterministic pre-trade risk limits before it is submitted. No path reaches a venue adapter or the simulator without a Risk Gate verdict. |  | integration: Every code path that can submit an order or transfer is enumerated and driven, each one is shown to obtain a gate verdict first, and an action with no verdict cannot be submitted. Preferably this is structural: the submit seam accepts only a gate-approved type. | v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map; v11.6 p22 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-007 | P1 | capability | **Post-trade risk management** — Risk management covers post-trade risk: after execution, positions, exposure and limits are re-evaluated from the fills, cancels and settlement events that actually occurred, not only before an order is sent. |  | integration: A fill that differs from the one the pre-trade check assumed (partial, slipped or gapped) is driven through, and the post-trade evaluation reflects the actual fill and reports a limit breach that the pre-trade check could not have seen. | v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map |
| RISK-008 | P1 | capability | **Market risk domain** — The risk model covers market risk: exposure to price, volatility, gaps, basis, greeks, factors and causal drivers. |  | unit: For a book with known sensitivities, each listed market exposure (price, volatility, gap, basis, greeks, factor, causal-driver) is computed to the expected value, and a limit keyed on each one can refuse an order. | v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map; v11.6 p22 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-009 | P1 | capability | **Liquidity risk domain** — The risk model covers liquidity risk: depth, time-to-exit, market impact, crowded exit, and quote and borrow availability. |  | unit: Given order-book depth, a position and borrow and quote availability, time-to-exit and impact are computed to expected values, a crowded exit (many holders of the same position) raises the estimate, and unavailable quotes or borrow are represented as such rather than as zero cost. | v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map; v11.6 p22 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-010 | P1 | capability | **Counterparty and venue risk domain** — The risk model covers counterparty and venue risk: credit, custody, exchange, bridge, broker and settlement exposure to each counterparty and venue. |  | unit: For a book spread across several venues, custodians, bridges and brokers with unsettled legs, exposure is attributed to each counterparty and venue in each listed category, and the per-entity totals reconcile to the book. | v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map; v11.6 p22 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-011 | P1 | capability | **Capital risk domain** — The risk model covers capital risk: leverage, margin, collateral, concentration, funding and liquidity buffers. |  | unit: For a book with known margin terms, collateral and funding, each listed capital measure is computed to the expected value, concentration is reported by the dimensions it is measured on, and a buffer below its floor is reported as a breach. | v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map; v11.6 p23 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-012 | P1 | capability | **Model risk domain** — The risk model covers model risk: drift, calibration, regime mismatch, uncertainty, feature failure and adversarial inputs. |  | replay: A replay that introduces a regime shift, a drifted feature, a failed feature and a crafted adversarial input raises a model-risk finding in the matching category for each one, and an unaltered replay raises none. | v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map; v11.6 p23 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-013 | P1 | capability | **Data risk domain** — The risk model covers data risk: stale, poisoned, manipulated, missing and inconsistent sources. |  | integration: Each defect class (stale, poisoned, manipulated, missing, inconsistent) is injected into a source feed. Each one is detected, attributed to the source it came from, and represented as data risk on the decisions that consumed it. | v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map; v11.6 p23 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-014 | P1 | capability | **Operational risk domain** — The risk model covers operational risk: node, network, clock, deployment, credential, reconciliation and dependency failure. |  | chaos: Each failure class (node, network, clock skew, bad deployment, expired or revoked credential, reconciliation break, dependency outage) is injected and appears in the operational risk state under its own category while the fault lasts. | v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map; v11.6 p23 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-015 | P1 | capability | **Systemic risk domain** — The risk model covers systemic risk: contagion across assets, regions and counterparties, and correlated causal mechanisms. | `MULTI_REGION` | replay: For a book whose positions in different assets, regions and counterparties share a causal mechanism, a replayed contagion episode shows the systemic measure aggregating them while each per-asset, per-region and per-counterparty measure alone stays inside its limit. | v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map; v11.6 p23 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-016 | P1 | capability | **Risk Brain forecasts risk** — The Risk Brain produces risk forecasts: forward-looking estimates of the book's risk, distinct from the Risk Gate's evaluation of present state against limits. |  | replay: Forecasts issued at each point of a replay are scored against the risk that was later realised, and the calibration is recorded per forecast horizon. | v11.6 p16 §9.1 Specialist Brain Society; v11.6 p22 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-017 | P1 | capability | **Risk Brain generates scenarios and stress tests** — The Risk Brain generates scenarios and stress tests and evaluates the book under them. |  | integration: A generated scenario applied to a fixed book yields a loss estimate per scenario, and re-running from the recorded scenario definition reproduces the same estimate. | v11.6 p16 §9.1 Specialist Brain Society; GCP v2.1 p9 §8 Regional GKE Service Plane |
| RISK-018 | P1 | capability | **Risk Brain issues risk recommendations** — The Risk Brain produces risk recommendations derived from its forecasts and scenarios, and each recommendation can be traced to the forecast or scenario that motivated it. |  | integration: Every recommendation the Risk Brain emits carries a reference to the forecast or scenario it derives from, and that reference resolves to a recorded forecast or scenario. | v11.6 p16 §9.1 Specialist Brain Society |
| RISK-019 | P0 | invariant | **Hard limits are enforced by deterministic gates** — Hard risk limits are enforced by deterministic gates. The Risk Gate's verdict is a pure function of the proposed action, the local state and the loaded limit set, and involves no model inference. |  | property: For generated (action, local state, limit set) triples, repeated evaluation, across process restarts included, returns an identical verdict, and the gate's dependency graph contains no model or inference component. | v11.6 p16 §9.1 Specialist Brain Society; v11.6 p22 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-020 | P0 | invariant | **Risk Brain has no enforcement authority** — The Risk Brain forecasts and the Risk Gate enforces. No Risk Brain output approves or vetoes an executable action directly. Its outputs reach enforcement only as limits or envelopes that the deterministic gate evaluates, and the hard pre-trade veto is never delegated to the Risk Brain. |  | integration: Gate verdicts on a fixed set of actions and states are unchanged when the Risk Brain is absent, stalled, or emitting recommendations that contradict the limits, and no interface lets a Brain output admit an action the gate refused. | v11.6 p22 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate; GCP v2.1 p9 §8 Regional GKE Service Plane |
| RISK-021 | P1 | capability | **Risk Brain discovers hidden concentration** — The Risk Brain uses AI, causal and scenario models to discover hidden concentration: exposure concentrated through a shared driver, counterparty or mechanism that no single instrument, venue or strategy limit reveals. |  | integration: In a constructed book whose positions each sit inside their own limits but share one causal driver, the Risk Brain flags the concentration and names the driver. A control book of the same size without the shared driver is not flagged. | v11.6 p22 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-022 | P1 | capability | **Risk Brain discovers emerging risk** — The Risk Brain uses AI, causal and scenario models to discover emerging risk: risk that is building before any deterministic limit is breached. |  | replay: Across replayed episodes that ended in a limit breach, the Risk Brain raised an emerging-risk finding before the breach, and the lead time is recorded. Across quiet periods, the false-positive rate is measured and reported. | v11.6 p22 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-023 | P0 | invariant | **Hard pre-trade veto is local and uses local state** — The hard pre-trade veto runs in the local Reflex node and evaluates its deterministic limits using only locally available state. No synchronous call to the Risk Brain, any regional service, the Fabric or another region sits between an action and its verdict. |  | chaos: With the Fabric, the Risk Brain and every regional service made unreachable or stalled, the Reflex gate still returns a verdict for every action, those verdicts are identical to the ones returned with everything reachable, and no verdict waits on the stalled side. | v11.6 p22 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate; GCP v2.1 p9 §8 Regional GKE Service Plane |
| RISK-024 | P2 | capability | **Conduct risk domain** — The risk model covers conduct risk: market-conduct and manipulation risk in the platform's own orders and quotes. |  | replay: Replayed order and quote sequences with known manipulative shapes (wash trading, spoofing, layering) are flagged as conduct risk, and ordinary sequences of the same volume are not. | v11.6 p23 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-025 | P3 | capability | **Intervention risk domain** — The risk model covers intervention risk for actions taken in the external world: truthfulness, disclosure, identity, communications permissions, causal overclaiming, unintended externalities and action-channel compromise. |  | unit: A proposed intervention that lacks disclosure, uses an unverified identity, uses a channel without permission, claims an effect beyond its evidence, or arrives over a compromised action channel is scored under the matching intervention-risk category, and a compliant proposal is not. | v11.6 p23 §14 Risk Brain + Deterministic Risk Gate |
| RISK-026 | P1 | placement | **Risk Brain placed on Regional GKE** — The Risk Brain runs as a warm regional service on Regional GKE Standard. | `KUBERNETES` | infra-plan: A plan for each region shows the Risk Brain workload on that region's regional GKE Standard cluster and shows no Risk Brain component on the Reflex node. | GCP v2.1 p9 §8 Regional GKE Service Plane |
| RISK-027 | P1 | capability | **Risk Brain generates risk envelopes** — The Risk Brain generates risk envelopes: the bounded limit sets handed to regional execution, which the local deterministic gate enforces. |  | integration: Once a Reflex gate loads an envelope produced by the Risk Brain, the gate refuses an action outside the envelope, admits one inside it, and records the envelope version that produced each verdict. | GCP v2.1 p9 §8 Regional GKE Service Plane |
| RISK-028 | P0 | failure_behavior | **Reconciliation break raises a P0/P1 Fabric event** — A reconciliation discrepancy between venue or custody truth and the ledger creates a P0/P1 event on the Fabric. |  | integration: When a venue or custody position that disagrees with the ledger is injected, a reconciliation-break event is published on the Fabric in the P0/P1 priority class, carrying both values and the direction of the difference. When they agree, no event is published. | GCP v2.1 p11 §10 Ledger/Capital/Financial State |
| RISK-029 | P0 | failure_behavior | **Reconciliation break narrows or stops local execution** — A reconciliation discrepancy can narrow or stop local execution, and deterministic policy decides whether to narrow or stop. |  | integration: Each discrepancy class in the policy is driven through, and the local cell's execution is narrowed or halted exactly as the policy specifies. The same discrepancy always produces the same response, and a discrepancy within tolerance leaves execution untouched, which proves the policy does not stop everything. | GCP v2.1 p11 §10 Ledger/Capital/Financial State |
| RISK-030 | P0 | prohibition | **Redis is never position or capital truth** — Redis is never the source of truth for positions or capital. Any Redis copy is a cache, and losing it or letting it go stale cannot change an authoritative position or capital figure. |  | chaos: Flushing or corrupting the Redis cache leaves every ledger position and capital balance unchanged, and no code path writes authoritative position or capital state from a Redis value. | GCP v2.1 p23 §28 Explicit Anti-Patterns |
| RISK-031 | P0 | prohibition | **Risk Gate never depends on Redis** — The Risk Gate never requires Redis. It produces verdicts with Redis unavailable, whether Redis is local or remote. |  | chaos: With Redis unreachable or absent, the gate returns verdicts identical to those it returns with Redis reachable, for the same actions and state. | GCP v2.1 p23 §28 Explicit Anti-Patterns |
| RISK-032 | P1 | capability | **Risk Brain publishes control events on the Fabric** — The Risk Brain publishes its outputs to regional execution as control-class events on the regional Fabric. |  | integration: A Risk Brain output, such as an envelope change, is published on the regional Fabric with the control event class and is consumed from there by the regional cell. | diagram pL178-184 §02 Regional Cell (edges) |
| RISK-033 | P1 | capability | **Capital/Treasury publishes control events on the Fabric** — The Capital/Treasury service publishes its outputs to regional execution as control-class events on the regional Fabric. |  | integration: A Capital/Treasury output, such as a capital grant change, is published on the regional Fabric with the control event class and is consumed from there by the regional cell. | diagram pL178-184 §02 Regional Cell (edges) |
| RISK-034 | P1 | capability | **Asset/Strategy publishes control events on the Fabric** — The Asset/Strategy service publishes its outputs to regional execution as control-class events on the regional Fabric. |  | integration: An Asset/Strategy output, such as a strategy activation or resize, is published on the regional Fabric with the control event class and is consumed from there by the regional cell. | diagram pL178-184 §02 Regional Cell (edges) |

Ledger, accounting, settlement, reconciliation.

## DATA

Scout fabric, source manifests, pass-through data, knowledge tiers, storage.

| ID | P | Kind | Requirement | Flags | Verification | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DATA-001 | P0 | prohibition | **No raw external-world corpus is ever retained** — External world content (web pages, filings, news, social and public discussion, product pages, regulatory records, geospatial feeds and other third-party sources) is never stored durably in raw form, in any store. Durable storage begins at the knowledge boundary, not the document boundary. There is no general-purpose raw-world-data lake, no copied document set and no web archive. |  | integration: A fixture source carrying a unique marker string is driven through the whole pipeline, then every durable sink the pipeline writes (manifests, K0-K3 stores, knowledge packs, the event log) is searched for the marker and for the payload's bytes, and the test fails if any sink holds more than the allow-listed derived fields of DATA-005. | v11.6 p3 §1.3 External World Data Is Pass-Through; Knowledge Is Durable (opening paragraph); v11.6 p12 §6 Global Scout & Data Acquisition Fabric (intro: 'The goal is not to hoard the internet'); v11.6 p12 §6.3 Pass-Through Acquisition and Knowledge Distillation ('Durable storage begins at the knowledge boundary, not the document boundary'); v11.6 p35 §26 Platform & Deployment Architecture, placement table, row 'Tick archive + replay' ('never retained as a raw corpus'); GCP v2.1 p2 §1 Executive Architecture (intro: 'persists only compact derived knowledge plus provenance references'); GCP v2.1 p2 §2.1 World Data Pass-Through / Knowledge Persistence Invariant (intro); GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules, rule 7 'State ownership is explicit' ('external world payloads are transient'); GCP v2.1 p10 §9.1 Pass-Through World Sensing Pipeline ('intentionally no general-purpose raw-world-data lake'); GCP v2.1 p17 §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog, row 'Cloud Storage' ('External world payloads are not retained'); diagram pL77 World-data rule notice |
| DATA-002 | P1 | process | **Pass-through acquisition runs as one ordered pipeline** — Every acquisition of external content passes through these stages in this order: source (API, web or feed); secure web/API egress; transient fetch in a scout worker; parse/extract; evidence/provenance check; entity/event/fact/feature extraction; knowledge delta; world models and memory. No stage may be skipped. In particular, no extracted content becomes knowledge without passing the evidence check. |  | integration: A fixture source is fetched end to end and the recorded stage trace shows every stage in the stated order. A second fixture whose evidence check fails produces no knowledge delta. | v11.6 p3 §1.3 (opening paragraph: 'The system extracts evidence and knowledge'); v11.6 p12 §6.3 Pass-Through Acquisition and Knowledge Distillation (pipeline diagram); GCP v2.1 p9 §9.1 Pass-Through World Sensing Pipeline (pipeline diagram) |
| DATA-003 | P0 | contract | **Every fetch writes a source manifest record sufficient to re-fetch** — Every fetch of an external source writes a Source Manifest record. The record carries: the canonical URI or provider ID and the provider/source identity; retrieval time; version/etag when the source supplies one; a cryptographic hash/fingerprint; entitlement; geography; cursor; freshness/expiry; parser/version lineage; and re-fetch instructions. The record holds no copy of the source body. |  | property: For arbitrary fixture fetches, each fetch produces exactly one manifest record. Every listed field is populated, with etag allowed empty only when the source supplies none. The stored hash equals the hash of the fetched bytes, and no field of the record holds the body. | v11.6 p3 §1.3 (opening paragraph 'records how to find the source again'; bullet 'Persist the source reference...'); v11.6 p12 §6.3 (pipeline branch 'SOURCE MANIFEST + HASH + CURSOR'); GCP v2.1 p2 §2.1, 'Source Manifest Registry' bullet; GCP v2.1 p9 §9.1 (pipeline branch 'SOURCE MANIFEST / HASH / CURSOR'); diagram pL238 VIEWS.data, 04 World Sensing, Tick History & Durable Knowledge, node 'source' ('URI · hash · etag · cursor') |
| DATA-004 | P0 | security_control | **The raw external payload is discarded as soon as processing ends** — An external source payload exists only long enough to be parsed, validated, extracted and reasoned over, whether or not processing produced a knowledge delta. The pipeline has a mandatory discard stage, wired from knowledge-delta creation as a security control, that removes the payload from memory and ephemeral disk. A pipeline assembled without that stage is refused. |  | integration: With the payload held in an instrumented buffer and an ephemeral file, one successful fetch and one fetch that fails at parse are run. After each, the test asserts that the buffer is released and the file is deleted, and that a pipeline built without the discard stage fails to construct. | v11.6 p3 §1.3 (opening paragraph: 'then discards the external content'); v11.6 p12 §6.3 (branch 'RAW EXTERNAL CONTENT DISCARDED'; 'External source payloads exist only long enough to parse, validate, extract and reason over them'); GCP v2.1 p2 §2.1 (intro: 'the source payload is then discarded'); GCP v2.1 p9 §9.1 (branch 'RAW PAYLOAD DISCARDED'); diagram pL243 VIEWS.data, 04, node 'discard' ('Discard Raw External Payload', marked 'required'); diagram pL257-261 VIEWS.data, 04, edge delta -> discard (class 'security') |
| DATA-005 | P0 | contract | **Only allow-listed compact knowledge types persist from world data** — Only these types persist from external world data: source manifests and hashes; normalized facts, entities, relationships, events and causal edges; embeddings/features; summaries; beliefs, with confidence, contradictions and novelty; timestamps; world-model and knowledge deltas; and memory episodes. A durable record derived from world data whose type is not on this list is refused. |  | unit: The durable write seam for world-derived records accepts each allow-listed type and refuses a record of any other type. A test enumerates the types the seam accepts and compares them with this list, failing on any difference. | v11.6 p3 §1.3, bullet 'Persist compact knowledge'; GCP v2.1 p10 §9.1 ('The durable plane stores only Algorik's compact interpretation of the world and the metadata required to revisit the source'); diagram pL77 World-data rule notice (the retained-artifact list) |
| DATA-006 | P1 | invariant | **Historical world analysis re-fetches the source through its manifest** — When historical reasoning needs external content again, it re-fetches that content from the original source or provider using the source's manifest, then processes it transiently again under DATA-004. The manifest's metadata (URI/provider ID, hash, etag, cursor) drives the re-fetch. A retained copy of the content never does. |  | integration: A fixture source is fetched and the pipeline discards it. The test then requests historical analysis of that source and asserts that a new fetch was made to the fixture origin using the manifest's URI and cursor, and that no stored copy was read. | v11.6 p3 §1.3, bullet 'Historical reasoning re-fetches the original source or licensed historical API using its manifest'; v11.6 p35 §26 placement table, row 'Tick archive + replay' ('re-fetched from its origin/provider when needed'); GCP v2.1 p3 §2.1, 'Historical world analysis' bullet; diagram pL257-261 VIEWS.data, 04, edge source -> scout (control, 're-fetch manifest') |
| DATA-007 | P0 | prohibition | **Licensed historical APIs are queried on demand, never bulk-copied** — Where a licensed provider exposes a historical API, historical analysis queries it on demand through the manifest, only for what the analysis needs. The provider's corpus is never copied. |  | integration: Against a fixture historical provider that counts requests, an analysis over a bounded window requests only that window. Afterwards, the only things written are derived knowledge and manifest entries. | v11.6 p3 §1.3, bullet 'Historical reasoning' ('or licensed historical API using its manifest'); GCP v2.1 p3 §2.1, 'Historical world analysis' bullet ('query them on demand rather than copying their whole corpus'); diagram pL235 VIEWS.data, 04, node 'hist' ('Historical world data requested on demand') |
| DATA-008 | P1 | failure_behavior | **Knowledge from unretrievable evidence is kept and marked no longer re-fetchable** — If the original content behind a piece of knowledge can no longer be retrieved, the derived knowledge is kept, and the fact that its evidence is no longer re-fetchable is recorded against it. |  | integration: A fixture source is fetched and distilled, then removed from its origin. The re-fetch attempt fails. The test asserts that the derived knowledge is still present and now carries a not-re-fetchable marker that its consumers can see. | v11.6 p3 §1.3, bullet 'Historical reasoning' ('If the original content cannot be retrieved, Algorik still retains the derived knowledge plus the fact that the evidence is no longer re-fetchable') |
| DATA-009 | P0 | invariant | **Tick/order-book data and internal financial records are their own retention classes** — High-rate tick/order-book market data and Algorik's own financial/execution records are distinct retention classes. Each is separate from pass-through world data and has its own retention policy. On the storage map they form Tier T (governed history), which is separate from knowledge tiers K0-K3. |  | unit: Every retained record type maps to exactly one retention class. The tick/order-book class and the internal financial/execution class are distinct values from the world-knowledge class, and a record with no class is refused at the write seam. | v11.6 p4 §1.3, bullet 'High-rate tick/order-book data and Algorik's own financial/execution records are separate retention classes'; GCP v2.1 p3 §2.1, bullet 'Tick/order-book and Algorik-owned financial/execution data are distinct retention classes'; GCP v2.1 p10 §9.2 Durable Knowledge Tiers, 'Tier T - retained market/internal history'; diagram pL77 World-data rule notice ('Tick/internal financial history has a separate governed retention policy'); diagram pL244-249 VIEWS.data, 04, tier map (node 'tick': 'T governed history') |
| DATA-010 | P0 | invariant | **Tick and execution data are retained only where rights, law and policy allow** — Tick/order-book data and Algorik's own financial/execution records are retained only when venue rights (entitlements), legal obligations and policy allow it. A request to retain data whose entitlement does not allow storage is refused. |  | integration: Two fixture venues are set up, one whose entitlement allows historical storage and one whose entitlement forbids it. Archiving the same event shape succeeds for the first and, for the second, is refused with an error naming the entitlement. | v11.6 p4 §1.3, bullet 'They may be retained when venue rights, legal obligations and policy allow'; GCP v2.1 p3 §2.1, bullet 'can be archived when rights/policy require replay, accounting, audit or model training'; GCP v2.1 p10 §9.2, 'Tier T' ('under entitlements and policy'); diagram pL248 VIEWS.data, 04, node 'tick' ('under rights/policy') |
| DATA-011 | P1 | capability | **Ambient source watchers track change with cursors and fingerprints, not copies** — For each watched source, an ambient source watcher keeps a cursor, the last-seen fingerprint and the knowledge deltas derived since. The platform therefore knows continuously what is changing without keeping the source corpus. |  | integration: A watcher over a fixture source detects an edit through a change of fingerprint, advances its cursor and emits a knowledge delta. Afterwards it holds no copy of either version of the body. | v11.6 p4 §1.3, bullet 'Ambient source watchers maintain cursors, last-seen fingerprints and knowledge deltas' |
| DATA-012 | P1 | nfr | **The durable knowledge layer is smaller and cheaper than the source data** — The durable knowledge derived from world data is smaller than the source content it was derived from, and cheaper to keep. It holds structured graph state, compact packs, vectors/features, summaries and episodic memory, not copied documents or web archives. |  | benchmark: Over a fixed fixture campaign, the bytes durably written for world data (manifests, K0-K3, packs) are measured against the bytes fetched. | DATA-013 | P1 | contract | **Knowledge packs are compact protobuf/Parquet artifacts** — Knowledge packs are compressed, compact protobuf/Parquet artifacts. | DATA-014 | P1 | invariant | **The Scout Fabric runs continuously and needs no human to add a feed** — The Scout Fabric operates continuously. | DATA-015 | P1 | capability | **Each source is scored on information gain, timeliness, reliability and realized contribution** — Every registered source is scored on incremental (unique) predictive information gain, timeliness, reliability and realized strategy contribution (source alpha), and each source's score is recorded over time. |  | replay: A fixture history is replayed with one informative source and one source that duplicates it. The scorer gives the duplicate near-zero incremental information gain and gives the informative source a positive realized contribution. | v11.6 p5 §2, row 'Data discovery finds sources' ('scores novelty', 'measures source alpha'); v11.6 p12 §6 ('measures whether they add unique predictive information'); v11.6 p13 §6.2 Discovery Agent Loop, step 5 |
| DATA-016 | P0 | invariant | **Every candidate source is inspected, including law and terms, before registration** — Before a candidate source is registered, it is inspected for access method, law/terms (access rights), schema, freshness, cost, expected uniqueness and manipulation risk. It is refused, with an error naming the attribute, when any attribute is missing or the law/terms evaluation is negative. | v11.6 p5 §2, row 'Data discovery finds sources' ('validates access rights'); v11.6 p12 §6.2 Discovery Agent Loop, step 3 |
| DATA-017 | P1 | capability | **The Scout Fabric creates or proposes adapters for approved sources** — For an approved source, the Scout Fabric creates the feed adapter or proposes one. |  | integration: For a fixture source with a documented schema, the fabric emits an adapter or an adapter proposal. The adapter parses a sample record into the canonical form, and the result is registered against the source. | v11.6 p5 §2, row 'Data discovery finds sources' ('creates adapters'); v11.6 p12 §6 ('creates or proposes adapters') |
| DATA-018 | P1 | capability | **Sources are promoted, throttled, quarantined or retired automatically under policy** — According to its score and access status, each source is promoted, throttled, quarantined or retired automatically under policy. |  | integration: Three fixture sources are set up: one scored below the retirement threshold, one flagged for manipulation, and one scored above the promotion threshold. | DATA-019 | P1 | capability | **Sensing covers every listed access method and source family** — Global sensing discovers and ingests over web, API, WebSocket, file, stream, database and registry access methods. | DATA-020 | P1 | capability | **The Scout Fabric searches for new lawful sources** — The Scout Fabric actively searches for new sources whose use is lawful, instead of working only from a fixed list. |  | integration: A discovery run over a fixture index that contains both new lawful and new unlawful candidates proposes the lawful ones for inspection, and no unlawful candidate reaches registration. | v11.6 p12 §6 ('It searches for new lawful sources') |

| DATA-025 | P1 | capability | **The source universe includes filings and public records** — The source universe includes filings, earnings, regulatory portals, court/docket data, procurement, patents, corporate registries, government statistics and central-bank releases. |  | integration: A fixture from each listed family passes through the pass-through pipeline and yields at least one knowledge delta with a manifest, and no raw document is retained. | v11.6 p12 §6.1 Source Universe, second bullet |
| DATA-026 | P1 | capability | **The source universe includes news and the public web** — The source universe includes news, press releases, expert publications, the public web, deep-web databases, public social signals and public discussion communities. |  | integration: A fixture from each listed family passes through the pass-through pipeline and yields at least one knowledge delta with a manifest, and no raw page is retained. | v11.6 p12 §6.1 Source Universe, third bullet |
| DATA-027 | P1 | capability | **The source universe includes blockchain state and flows** — The source universe includes blockchain state, mempools, token flows, smart-contract events and protocol governance. |  | integration: A fixture chain feed that includes a block, a pending transaction, a token transfer, a contract event and a governance proposal yields one normalized event of each kind, with a manifest. | v11.6 p12 §6.1 Source Universe, fourth bullet |

| DATA-030 | P0 | invariant | **Licensed and user-authorized sources are admitted only under explicit entitlements** — Private, alternative and licensed datasets, and sources a user has authorized, are admitted only under explicit entitlements. |  | integration: A fixture user-authorized source with no entitlement record is refused. ## EVID

Evidence, provenance and truth fabric.

| ID | P | Kind | Requirement | Flags | Verification | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EVID-001 | P0 | contract | **Every processed world source leaves a manifest record with its provenance and lineage** — For every external world source Algorik processes, persist a manifest record carrying: the source reference, the provider/source identity, the retrieval timestamp, the version or etag when the source supplies one, a cryptographic hash/fingerprint of the content retrieved, the entitlement it was retrieved under, its geography, the parser and parser-version lineage that processed it, and its freshness/expiry metadata. A record missing any of these fields is refused, except version/etag, whose absence is recorded explicitly as not supplied by the source rather than left empty. |  | unit: Constructing a manifest record with each mandatory field removed in turn is refused with an error naming that field; a complete record round-trips through serialisation unchanged; a record without version/etag is admitted only when it states explicitly that the source supplied none. | v11.6 p3 §1.3 External World Data Is Pass-Through; Knowledge Is Durable |
| EVID-002 | P1 | process | **Historical reasoning re-fetches the source through its manifest** — When historical reasoning needs the content behind a past piece of evidence, it re-fetches that content from the original source, or from a licensed historical API, using the source's manifest record. It never reads a retained copy of the external payload. |  | integration: A historical query over a fixture claim, run with no copy of the payload available anywhere, succeeds by issuing a fetch whose target and version come from the claim's manifest record, and it reports the fetched bytes' hash against the manifest hash. | v11.6 p3 §1.3 External World Data Is Pass-Through; Knowledge Is Durable |
| EVID-003 | P1 | failure_behavior | **Knowledge survives a source that can no longer be fetched, and says so** — If the original external content can no longer be retrieved, Algorik keeps the knowledge derived from it and records on that source's manifest that the evidence is no longer re-fetchable, with when the failure was observed and its cause. The derived knowledge is neither deleted nor presented as re-verifiable. |  | integration: With a fixture source made unretrievable (page removed, licence expired, API retired), a re-fetch attempt leaves every derived fact and belief intact, marks the manifest non-re-fetchable with a timestamp and cause, and a later query over that knowledge returns the marker. | v11.6 p3 §1.3 External World Data Is Pass-Through; Knowledge Is Durable |
| EVID-004 | P1 | contract | **An evidence score is separate components, not one data-confidence number** — Evidence/Provenance scores every evidence item on separate components, at least corroboration, contradiction, source quality and freshness, and keeps each component on the item. Confidence in a claim is derived from those components. It is never taken from a single source-supplied or ingest-time 'data confidence' value. |  | unit: Every scored evidence item exposes the four components individually; recomputing a claim's confidence from them reproduces the stored value; the scorer's output type cannot represent an evidence item that carries only a scalar confidence. | v11.6 p5 §2 Corrections Required to v10.1 — 'Data confidence is enough' row; v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map — 'Evidence & trust' row; v11.6 p42 §31 Capability Completeness Checklist; diagram pL241 VIEWS.data — 04 · World Sensing, Tick History & Durable Knowledge (node 'ev') |
| EVID-005 | P1 | capability | **Evidence forms a provenance graph a belief can be traced through** — The Evidence/Truth Fabric builds a provenance graph in which each Evidence object is linked to its source manifest, to the evidence it corroborates or contradicts, and to the beliefs it updated, so that every belief can be traced back to the full set of evidence and sources it rests on. |  | integration: For a belief built from a fixture of claims across several sources, traversing the graph from the belief returns exactly the fixture's Evidence objects and their manifests, with none missing and none extra, and recomputing the belief from that set alone reproduces the stored belief. | v11.6 p5 §2 Corrections Required to v10.1 — 'Data confidence is enough' row; v11.6 p6 §3 Full Capability Map — 'Evidence & trust' row; v11.6 p13 §7 Evidence, Provenance & Truth Fabric (intro) |
| EVID-006 | P0 | invariant | **Corroboration counts independent origins, not copies** — Corroboration is measured as agreement among independent sources, weighted by their common-source dependence. | EVID-007 | P0 | invariant | **Contradictions are kept as competing hypotheses, never deleted** — When evidence conflicts, the contradiction engine keeps each side as a competing hypothesis with its own supporting evidence. ## REASON

Symbolic and neuro-symbolic reasoning fabric.

| ID | P | Kind | Requirement | Flags | Verification | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REASON-001 | P0 | invariant | **Symbolic conclusions never violate a declared invariant** — The symbolic reasoners hold their invariants explicitly, as a declared and versioned set, and preserve them. No conclusion, derivation or compiled artifact the fabric emits may violate a declared invariant. A reasoning step that would violate one is refused, and the refusal names the invariant. |  | property: Generate random fact sets against a fixture of declared invariants. Assert that no emitted conclusion violates any invariant and that every refused step names the invariant it would have broken. Then remove one invariant from the set and assert that a conclusion violating it now appears, which proves the check can fire. | v11.6 p2 §1 Executive Summary ('symbolic reasoners preserve explicit invariants and proof traces') |
| REASON-002 | P0 | invariant | **Consequential conclusions carry a machine-readable derivation** — Every conclusion the fabric emits that can reach a proposal, a promotion gate, a risk or capital decision, or the event log carries a machine-readable derivation artifact with four parts: the proof trace (the rules, constraints and graph paths applied), the evidence set it rests on, the assumptions it found violated, and its uncertainty. Free-form prose alone is not a derivation. |  | replay: Replay a recorded reasoning run from the event log. | GOV-024 | P2 | process | **A validated cognitive result becomes a strategy, model, risk or capital proposal** — A validated result of the world-event-to-cognitive-response flow is emitted as a strategy, model, risk or capital proposal. |  | integration: Driving a world event through the flow end to end in simulation produces a typed strategy, model, risk or capital proposal record linked to the validated result and evidence it came from. | GCP v2.1 p20 §21.2 World event to cognitive response, step 5 ('Validated result becomes a strategy/model/risk/capital proposal') |
| GOV-025 | P0 | invariant | **Proposals reach the hot path only as signed packages through promotion gates** — Promotion gates convert an accepted proposal into a signed policy or model package. | GOV-026 | P0 | prohibition | **Autonomous agents cannot obtain production capital or custody authority** — No autonomous agent can obtain production capital authority or custody authority. |  | acceptance: Requests from each autonomous-agent identity to raise the autonomy ceiling, grant capital or perform a custody operation are refused; AutonomyController::request_change refuses any request without an authenticated operator identity; and no agent identity holds an IAM role on capital or custody resources. | GCP v2.1 p23 §27 Architecture Acceptance Criteria ('Autonomous agents cannot obtain production capital/custody authority') |
| GOV-027 | P0 | prohibition | **Autonomous agents cannot merge or deploy around policy** — No autonomous agent can merge a change or deploy an artifact except through the same policy-gated review, CI and promotion path that every other change takes. |  | game-day: In the agent-compromise simulation, an autonomous development agent given a malicious instruction tries to merge without required review, push to a protected branch and deploy an unattested digest. | GOV-028 | P0 | prohibition | **Autonomous agents cannot access long-lived cloud keys** — No autonomous agent can access a long-lived cloud key. |  | infra-plan: The plan declares no service-account key and no storage HMAC key, enforces the organization policy that disables service-account key creation, and grants agent and CI identities access only through Workload Identity Federation; ./scripts/check-secrets.sh reports nothing found. | GCP v2.1 p23 §27 Architecture Acceptance Criteria ('cannot access long-lived cloud keys') |

| OBS-026 | P1 | capability | **Network paths are observable through flow logs, connectivity tests, load-balancer telemetry and link metrics** — Network observability uses VPC Flow Logs where appropriate, Connectivity Tests and Network Intelligence Center tooling, load-balancer telemetry, and Interconnect/VPN metrics. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | infra-plan: The plan enables flow logs on the subnets that carry Reflex, Fabric and mesh traffic, declares Connectivity Tests for the venue, mesh and collector paths, and enables logging on every load balancer. | GCP v2.1 p14 §16 Observability, SRE and AIOps — Network bullet; GCP v2.1 p18 §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform — Network Intelligence Center / Connectivity Tests row |
| OBS-027 | P1 | slo | **Every plane and every dependency has its own SLOs** — SLOs are defined per plane and per dependency. |  | inspection: Every plane in the platform's plane list, and every declared dependency between planes, has at least one SLO with a target, a window and a source series. | GCP v2.1 p14 §16 Observability, SRE and AIOps — SLOs bullet ('per plane and dependency') |
| OBS-028 | P1 | process | **Error budgets drive release policy** — Each SLO carries an error budget, and the budget's state drives release policy for the plane it belongs to. |  | integration: With a fixture plane's error budget exhausted, the release pipeline refuses a promotion to that plane and records the budget as the reason. With budget remaining, the same promotion proceeds. | GCP v2.1 p14 §16 Observability, SRE and AIOps — SLOs bullet ('error budgets that drive release policy') |
| OBS-029 | P0 | slo | **Fabric backlog and ledger reconciliation are product SLOs** — Fabric backlog and ledger reconciliation are product SLOs, reported and owned with the product's objectives, not only as infrastructure metrics. |  | inspection: The product SLO catalogue (the one the desk-facing console reports) contains an objective on Fabric consumer backlog and an objective on reconciliation mismatch age, each with a target and a source series. | GCP v2.1 p14 §16 Observability, SRE and AIOps — SLOs bullet ('Fabric backlog and ledger reconciliation are product SLOs') |
| OBS-030 | P0 | invariant | **Every autonomous remediation action is audited** — Every rollback, restart, drain or scale action the SRE agent executes is recorded in an audit trail. |  | integration: After the agent executes a runbook action in a fixture, an append-only audit record exists naming the runbook, the triggering incident, the target resource and the result. | OBS-031 | P0 | slo | **Reflex SLOs: decision latency, venue round trip, book age, risk-gate latency, dropped feed messages** — Reflex has SLOs on market-event-to-decision latency at p99 and p99.9, venue round-trip time, stale-book age, local risk-gate latency and dropped feed messages. |  | benchmark: A Reflex cell at rated load on a recorded feed reports all five series. | OBS-032 | P0 | slo | **Fabric SLOs: quorum latency, availability, replication, consumer/mirror/archive lag, schema rejects** — The Fabric has SLOs on publish-quorum latency at p99, broker availability, partition under-replication, consumer lag, mirror lag, archive lag and schema reject rate. |  | chaos: In a three-broker test cluster, stopping one broker moves the under-replication and availability series. | OBS-033 | P1 | slo | **Warm-service SLOs: request latency and errors, saturation, pod disruption, circuit opens** — Warm services on GKE have SLOs on request p99 latency and error rate, saturation, pod disruption and dependency circuit-breaker opens. | `KUBERNETES` | chaos: In a test environment, killing a serving instance moves the disruption series and failing a dependency moves the circuit-open series. | OBS-034 | P0 | slo | **Ledger SLOs: commit latency, outcome-to-ledger lag, reconciliation mismatch age, abort rate** — The ledger has SLOs on Spanner commit latency at p99, outcome-to-ledger lag, reconciliation mismatch age and transaction abort rate. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | integration: Ledger writes are denied for a window (G p22 §25 'ledger outage'). Outcome-to-ledger lag rises during the window and returns to zero after idempotent catch-up. An injected unreconciled break makes mismatch age grow until it is resolved. | GCP v2.1 p15 §16 SLO table (Component: Ledger) |
| OBS-035 | P1 | slo | **Data SLOs: archive delay, re-fetch health, Bigtable latency, knowledge and BigQuery freshness, lineage completeness** — The data plane has SLOs on GCS retained-archive delay, source re-fetch health, Bigtable p99 latency, knowledge-delta freshness, BigQuery ingestion freshness and lineage completeness. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | integration: A data-plane fixture with a delayed archive upload, a failing source re-fetch and a record missing lineage moves the three corresponding series. Lineage completeness is reported as the share of records that have full lineage. | GCP v2.1 p15 §16 SLO table (Component: Data) |
| OBS-036 | P2 | slo | **AI SLOs: package freshness, calibration drift, training queue, tool failures, quantum-classical delta** — The AI plane has SLOs on model package freshness, calibration and drift, training/evaluation queue, agent tool failures and the quantum-versus-classical benchmark delta. |  | integration: Each of three faults moves its series: a model package held past its freshness bound, a calibration set with injected drift, and a quantum job run beside its classical baseline. The benchmark delta is reported with both arms. | GCP v2.1 p15 §16 SLO table (Component: AI) |
| OBS-037 | P0 | slo | **Delivery SLOs: lead time, rollback rate, reproducibility, attestation coverage, config drift, autonomous PR outcomes** — Delivery has SLOs on lead time, rollback rate, build reproducibility, attestation coverage, config drift and autonomous PR acceptance/rework rate. |  | integration: Delivery metrics computed from CI and deploy history report each objective. | OBS-038 | P0 | placement | **SLOs and alert policies are defined in Cloud Monitoring** — SLO definitions and alert policies are held in Cloud Monitoring. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | infra-plan: The plan declares a Cloud Monitoring SLO and an alert policy for each P0 objective. Each policy names a metric that a binary actually records outside tests. | GCP v2.1 p18 §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform — Cloud Monitoring row ('Metrics/SLOs/alerts') |
| OBS-039 | P0 | contract | **Collectors forward to the backends asynchronously over OTLP or Google APIs** — OpenTelemetry collectors forward telemetry to Cloud Monitoring, Managed Prometheus, Cloud Logging and Cloud Trace over OTLP or Google APIs, asynchronously. They sample and buffer so that a backend's slowness never reaches production workloads. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | chaos: The backend endpoint is made unreachable for a window. The collector buffers up to its bound and then samples or drops. Producers see no added latency or errors, and the buffered data arrives after the backend returns. | GCP v2.1 p19 §20 Critical Service-to-Service Connection Matrix — OTel collectors row |
| OBS-040 | P0 | contract | **OTel/AIOps telemetry enters the Fabric at QoS class P4** — Telemetry events from the OTel collectors and AIOps agents are published into the regional Fabric at QoS class P4, the lowest priority. |  | chaos: Under broker backpressure from a frozen sink, P4 telemetry is sampled or dropped oldest-first. | OBS-041 | P0 | contract | **Both promotion paths report their outcomes into Observability** — Both Argo Rollouts (warm services) and the Reflex Package Controller (Reflex VMs) report deployment and runtime outcomes into the Observability/SLO system. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` | e2e: In a test environment, one warm-service rollout and one Reflex package activation each produce an outcome record in the observability store. Each record is tagged with its artifact digest, cohort and result, and the rollout comparator reads it. | diagram pL364-366 §07 CI/CD, GitOps & Autonomous Development (edges roll->obs, pkg->obs) |

## CICD

CI/CD, supply chain, GitOps, autonomous development.

| ID | P | Kind | Requirement | Flags | Verification | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CICD-001 | P0 | process | **Every deploy passes five gates before promotion** — Every deploy runs simulation, integration, security, performance and paper-trading gates, and is promoted only when all five pass. |  | acceptance: The promotion policy names all five gates, and it refuses to promote an artifact that lacks any one gate verdict or carries a failing one. | v11.6 p41 §29 Autonomous Platform Operations / AIOps |
| CICD-002 | P0 | placement | **Engineering/Control plane runs on the named supply-chain services** — The Engineering/Control plane's primary runtime is GitHub, Cloud Build private pools, Artifact Registry, Config Sync, and Argo CD with Kargo and Argo Rollouts. | `MANAGED_SERVICE` `KUBERNETES` | infra-plan: Terraform and the workflow definitions place build, artifact storage and GitOps reconciliation on exactly these services, and no second build or deploy path exists beside them. | GCP v2.1 p2 §1 Executive Architecture — plane table, Engineering/Control row |
| CICD-003 | P0 | prohibition | **Deployments reference immutable digests, never mutable tags** — Every deployment reference names an immutable, signed artifact digest. No environment manifest, image reference or package pin refers to a mutable tag such as 'latest'. |  | acceptance: A scan of every environment manifest, Terraform image reference and package pin finds only digest references, and admission refuses a workload specified by tag. | GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 8; GCP v2.1 p23 §28 Explicit Anti-Patterns — mutable latest tags |
| CICD-004 | P0 | prohibition | **No console-only or undocumented emergency changes** — Every change to deployed infrastructure or configuration, including an emergency change, is declared in Git. No change exists only in a console or as undocumented emergency configuration. |  | game-day: Rebuilding an environment from Terraform, Git and artifacts alone reproduces its running configuration, and drift detection reports no resource whose state is undeclared in Git. | GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 8; GCP v2.1 p23 §28 Explicit Anti-Patterns — undocumented emergency config |
| CICD-005 | P0 | prohibition | **No hand-copied model files** — Model weights and manifests reach a runtime only as signed packages delivered through the supply chain. No model file is copied by hand onto a host or into a serving location. |  | inspection: Every model load path verifies a package signature, and a digest recorded in the environment repository. A model file placed out of band is refused at load. | GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 8; GCP v2.1 p23 §28 Explicit Anti-Patterns — hand-copied model files |
| CICD-006 | P0 | prohibition | **No secret values in Git** — No secret value is committed to any Git repository. Git carries only references to secrets held in the secret store. |  | acceptance: A secret scanner run over the full history of every repository finds nothing, and CI fails any commit that introduces a secret value. | GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 8 |
| CICD-007 | P0 | invariant | **Agent changes reach production only through the same gated pipeline** — Autonomous agents may open PRs, run experiments and diagnose incidents. Any production change they originate reaches production only through Git, tests, attestation, promotion policy and a rollback path, as a human change does. This includes changes to capital, risk and strategy packages and any capability change a Learning Agent proposes. |  | game-day: An agent-compromise simulation (G §25) gives an agent a malicious instruction. It confirms the agent cannot merge, promote or deploy without passing tests, attestation and promotion policy, and that every agent-originated deploy has a recorded rollback target. | GCP v2.1 p3 §2 Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules — Rule 9; GCP v2.1 p12 §13 Autonomous Development and AI Engineering — introduction; GCP v2.1 p12 §13 Autonomous Development agent roles — Learning Agent row (hard boundary); diagram pL393-395 §08 End-to-End Operating Flow (edges) — Autonomous Engineering → Capital/Risk/Strategy |
| CICD-008 | P0 | placement | **prod/engineering is the software supply-chain boundary** — Cloud Build private pools, Artifact Registry, signing/attestation and the GitOps management cluster live in the prod/engineering folder, and that folder forms the software supply-chain boundary. | `KUBERNETES` `MANAGED_SERVICE` | infra-plan: The Terraform plan creates each named resource in a prod/engineering project, and puts no build pool, registry, signing key or GitOps controller in any workload project. | GCP v2.1 p4 §4 GCP Organization, Folder and Project Model — prod/engineering row |
| CICD-009 | P0 | process | **GitOps ownership is split across four controllers** — Config Sync owns the cluster baseline, policies and CRDs. Argo CD owns applications. Kargo owns environment promotion. Argo Rollouts owns progressive rollout inside a target cluster. No object is owned by two of these controllers. | `KUBERNETES` | inspection: Every managed object carries exactly one owning controller, and the set of objects each controller manages matches its part of the split. | GCP v2.1 p9 §8 Regional GKE Service Plane — GitOps split |
| CICD-010 | P2 | capability | **Planner decomposes goals into a plan across the agent roles** — The Planner, the diagram's Agent Orchestrator, reads architecture, the repository, issues and telemetry. It decomposes a goal into work, allocates that work across coding, test/replay, security and architecture agents, and produces a plan. |  | integration: Given a scoped goal, the planner emits a plan in which each task is assigned to one of the four roles and traces back to the goal. | GCP v2.1 p12 §13 Autonomous Development agent roles — Planner row; diagram pL364-366 §07 CI/CD, GitOps & Autonomous Development (edges) — orch → code/test/secagent/archagent |
| CICD-011 | P0 | prohibition | **Planner cannot merge or deploy** — The Planner holds no permission to merge a change or to deploy an artifact. |  | inspection: The planner's identity has no merge right on any protected branch, no write access to the environment repository, and no deploy API permission. | GCP v2.1 p12 §13 Autonomous Development agent roles — Planner row (hard boundary) |

| CICD-013 | P0 | security_control | **Agent workers use scoped, sandboxed credentials with no production secrets** — Agent execution workers run under scoped service accounts, with sandboxed credentials that grant no access to production secrets. |  | game-day: An agent-compromise simulation confirms that a worker's service account cannot read any production secret, and that its IAM bindings are limited to its sandbox project. | GCP v2.1 p12 §13 Autonomous Development agent roles — Coder row (hard boundary); GCP v2.1 p12 §13 Autonomous Development and AI Engineering — Agent runtime bullet |
| CICD-014 | P2 | capability | **Test/Replay Agent runs the full test taxonomy against baselines** — The Test/Replay Agent runs unit, integration, property, fuzz, replay, performance and model tests, and compares the results against baselines. | `NEW_DEPENDENCY` | integration: For a change, the agent's evidence gives a result for each of the seven categories, plus a baseline comparison for the replay and performance results. | GCP v2.1 p12 §13 Autonomous Development agent roles — Test/Replay Agent row; diagram pL350 VIEWS.cicd — 07 · CI/CD, GitOps & Autonomous Development (node 'test') |
| CICD-015 | P0 | prohibition | **Test/Replay Agent cannot waive a failing risk or performance gate** — The Test/Replay Agent cannot waive a failing risk gate or a failing performance gate. |  | inspection: The gate configuration grants no agent identity an override, and a PR whose risk or performance gate failed cannot merge, whichever agent ran the gate. | GCP v2.1 p12 §13 Autonomous Development agent roles — Test/Replay Agent row (hard boundary) |

| CICD-017 | P0 | security_control | **Security finding severity controls promotion** — A severity policy over security findings decides promotion. | CICD-018 | P2 | capability | **Architecture Agent checks dependency, ownership and invariant rules** — The Architecture Agent checks dependency rules, hot-path violations, state and service ownership, latency and failure invariants, and conformance with ADRs. |  | integration: The agent flags, before merge, any change that breaks a seeded dependency rule, crosses a state-ownership boundary, or adds a blocking call on the hot path. | GCP v2.1 p12 §13 Autonomous Development agent roles — Architecture Agent row; diagram pL352 VIEWS.cicd — 07 · CI/CD, GitOps & Autonomous Development (node 'archagent') |
| CICD-019 | P0 | invariant | **No agent redefines a non-negotiable rule silently** — No agent changes or excepts a non-negotiable architecture rule silently. | COVERAGE-003 | P1 | capability | **Cash funding behind each position is represented** — The Cash/FX class must support funding: the cash allocated or borrowed to finance a position is represented with its currency, amount and cost, so that the funding behind any position can be read and is included in its valuation. |  | integration: Open a paper position financed in a second currency and assert the funding balance, its currency and its accrued cost are recorded against the position and appear in the position's valuation. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Cash / FX row |
| COVERAGE-004 | P1 | capability | **Equities, ETFs, baskets and indices are registrable** — The asset registry must represent listed equities, ETFs, baskets and indices as instruments; a basket or index references its constituents and their weights. |  | integration: Register a listed equity, an ETF, a basket and an index, and assert each round-trips through the registry and that the basket and the index resolve to their constituents with weights summing to one. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Equities / ETFs / indices row |
| COVERAGE-005 | P1 | capability | **Corporate actions adjust positions and history** — The platform must process corporate actions on equity-class instruments (for example splits, dividends, mergers, symbol changes and delistings), adjusting positions, cost basis, ledger cash and price history so that exposure and returns remain correct across the event. |  | replay: Replay a fixed tape spanning a stock split and a cash dividend on a paper position and assert quantity, cost basis and ledger cash change by the event's terms and that two replays of the same tape produce identical adjusted positions. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Equities / ETFs / indices row |
| COVERAGE-006 | P1 | capability | **Government, corporate and credit debt instruments are registrable** — The asset registry must represent government debt, corporate debt and credit instruments, carrying the terms that determine their cash flows (issuer, coupon, maturity and accrual convention). |  | integration: Register a government bond, a corporate bond and a credit instrument and assert each round-trips with its terms and that the projected cash-flow schedule matches the coupon and maturity it was registered with. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Rates / fixed income / credit row |
| COVERAGE-007 | P1 | capability | **Yield curves are built and cited by valuations** — The platform must build yield curves as market objects held with the as-of time they were built for, and every rates valuation must name the curve version it discounted with. |  | unit: Build a curve from a fixed set of quotes and assert it reprices the input instruments within a stated tolerance and that a valuation produced from it records the curve's version and as-of time. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Rates / fixed income / credit row |
| COVERAGE-008 | P1 | capability | **Repo and secured funding interfaces where a counterparty offers them** — Where a venue or counterparty offers repo or other secured funding, the platform must provide an interface to it so that rates positions can be financed against collateral; where none is offered, a request to use one is refused. | `LIVE_CAPITAL` | integration: Drive the repo interface against a simulated counterparty and assert a repo opens with collateral, rate and term recorded, that a request with no repo-offering counterparty configured is refused, and that the interface cannot be constructed against a live counterparty. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Rates / fixed income / credit row |
| COVERAGE-009 | P1 | capability | **Energy, metals, agricultural commodities and futures are registrable** — The asset registry must represent energy, metals and agricultural commodities, including commodity futures identified by product, delivery location and delivery period where the contract specifies them. |  | integration: Register one energy, one metal and one agricultural commodity plus two futures on the same product differing only in delivery month, and assert all round-trip and the two futures resolve to distinct instruments. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Commodities row |
| COVERAGE-010 | P1 | capability | **Commodity futures link to their spot or physical underlying** — Each commodity future must be linked to the spot or physical commodity it references, so that basis between futures and spot/physical prices can be computed and a physical holding can be related to its futures hedge. |  | integration: Register a future and its physical underlying and assert the link resolves in both directions and that basis computed from a fixed pair of prices equals their difference. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Commodities row |
| COVERAGE-011 | P1 | capability | **Commodity valuation includes shipping and storage economics** — Commodity valuation and feasibility must include shipping and storage economics - transport, storage and insurance costs over the holding period - so that a spot/futures or cross-location spread is judged net of carry, and an opportunity whose carry costs are unknown is refused rather than costed at zero. |  | unit: Value a cash-and-carry opportunity with fixed storage and shipping costs and assert the net result equals the gross spread minus those costs, then remove the storage cost and assert the opportunity is refused. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Commodities row |
| COVERAGE-012 | P1 | capability | **Options, futures, perpetuals and other derivative types are registrable** — The asset registry must represent options, futures, perpetuals and other derivative types, each linked to its underlying and carrying the contract terms that define it (for example expiry, strike, multiplier, or the funding mechanics of a perpetual). |  | integration: Register an option, a future and a perpetual on the same underlying and assert each round-trips with its terms and resolves to that underlying. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Derivatives row |
| COVERAGE-013 | P0 | constraint | **A derivative type without permission is refused at order creation** — A derivative type may be traded only when it is permitted for the trading entity and jurisdiction; a type without that permission remains available to research and simulation but is refused before an order object for it exists, and with no permissions configured every derivative type is refused. |  | acceptance: Register a derivative type with no permission and assert an order for it is refused before an order object exists while the same instrument can still be simulated, then grant the permission and assert the same order is admitted. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Derivatives row ('other permitted derivatives') |
| COVERAGE-014 | P1 | capability | **Derivative positions carry a margin model** — Derivative positions must carry a margin model - initial and maintenance margin under the applicable venue or clearing rules - so that the capital a derivative consumes is known before it is traded, and a position with no applicable margin rule is refused rather than margined at zero. |  | unit: Compute margin for a fixed option and future position against a fixed rule set and assert initial and maintenance margin equal hand-computed values, then remove the rule and assert the position is refused. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Derivatives row |
| COVERAGE-015 | P1 | capability | **Greeks are computed for option positions and aggregated per underlying** — The platform must compute greeks (delta, gamma, vega, theta and rho) for option positions and aggregate them per underlying, so that derivative risk is measured in sensitivities and not in notional alone. |  | property: For generated options, assert delta and gamma agree with finite-difference bumps of the pricing model within tolerance, and that aggregated delta per underlying equals the sum of the positions' deltas. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Derivatives row |
| COVERAGE-016 | P1 | capability | **Each derivative type carries a settlement model applied in the ledger** — Each derivative type must carry a settlement model - expiry, exercise, cash versus physical settlement, and periodic funding for perpetuals - and derivative positions must be settled by that model in the ledger. |  | integration: Carry a paper option to expiry both in and out of the money, a future to final settlement and a perpetual across a funding interval, and assert each posts exactly the ledger entries its settlement model dictates. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Derivatives row |
| COVERAGE-017 | P1 | capability | **Crypto spot, crypto derivatives and tokenized representations are registrable** — The asset registry must represent crypto spot assets, crypto derivatives and tokenized representations of other assets; a tokenized representation references the asset it represents and the chain and token contract it lives on. |  | integration: Register a crypto spot asset, a crypto perpetual and a tokenized representation of a registered bond, and assert each round-trips and the tokenized representation resolves to both the bond and its chain and token contract. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Crypto / tokenized row |
| COVERAGE-018 | P1 | capability | **Crypto and tokenized instruments trade through CEX and DEX venue adapters** — The platform must support trading crypto and tokenized instruments on centralised (CEX) and decentralised (DEX) venues, through a venue adapter of each type that reports orders and fills in the common execution contract. | `LIVE_CAPITAL` | integration: Drive a paper order through a simulated CEX adapter and a simulated DEX adapter and assert both produce fills in the common execution contract, and that neither adapter can be constructed with any autonomy ceiling other than paper trading. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Crypto / tokenized row |
| COVERAGE-019 | P1 | capability | **Cross-chain bridges are supported with cost, delay and counterparty risk modelled** — The platform must support moving tokenized assets between chains over bridges, modelling each bridge's fee, transfer delay and counterparty risk, and must not credit the destination balance before the modelled transfer completes. | `LIVE_CAPITAL` | integration: Simulate a bridge transfer and assert the source balance is debited at once, the destination is credited only after the modelled delay, the modelled fee is booked, and that no path exists to issue a transfer on a real bridge. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Crypto / tokenized row |
| COVERAGE-020 | P1 | capability | **On-chain settlement is reconciled against chain state** — The platform must support on-chain settlement of crypto and tokenized trades, treating a trade as settled only once chain state confirms it and recording a reconciliation break when chain state and the ledger disagree. | `LIVE_CAPITAL` | integration: Against a simulated chain, settle a paper trade and assert the ledger marks it settled only after the simulated confirmation, then diverge the simulated chain state and assert a reconciliation break is recorded. | v11.6 p26 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table, Crypto / tokenized row |
| COVERAGE-021 | P1 | capability | **Private and illiquid investments are registrable and valued from dated marks** — The asset registry must represent private equity, private credit, fund interests, real assets and other non-continuously priced investments, valued from dated marks rather than continuous quotes, with each mark's as-of time carried into every valuation that uses it. |  | integration: Register a private fund interest and a real asset each with a past-dated mark, and assert their valuations use that mark and report its as-of time and age, and that no continuous quote is synthesised for either. | v11.6 p27 §21 Asset & Market Coverage - class table (continued), Private/illiquid row |
| COVERAGE-022 | P1 | acceptance | **One asset-class registry holds every major class family** — A single asset-class registry must hold an entry for each major class family - liquid (the cash/FX, equity, rates, commodity and derivative classes of §21), event-driven, private/illiquid, tokenized and physical - and an instrument naming a class the registry does not hold is refused. |  | acceptance: Enumerate the registry and assert every class row of the §21 table has an entry, then register an instrument naming an unregistered class and assert it is refused. | v11.6 p43 §31 Capability Completeness Checklist - 'All major liquid, event-driven, private/illiquid, tokenized and physical classes have an extensible registry' |
| COVERAGE-023 | P1 | acceptance | **The asset-class registry is extensible without changing its consumers** — The asset-class registry must be extensible: a new class is added as a versioned registry entry, with its class-specific adapters and lifecycle engine plugged in, without changing the code of the components that consume the registry, and instruments registered under an earlier version continue to resolve unchanged. |  | acceptance: Add a test-only class in a new registry version and assert the valuation, risk and ledger paths accept an instrument of it with no code change to them, and that an instrument registered under the previous version still resolves to the same entry. | v11.6 p43 §31 Capability Completeness Checklist - 'All major liquid, event-driven, private/illiquid, tokenized and physical classes have an extensible registry' |
